GLP-1 SMA 10mg & 20mg Peptide Pens – Atlas Longevity Bali

What Is GLP-1 SMA?

GLP-1 SMA is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that acts on pathways involved in blood glucose regulation, appetite and gastric emptying.

It is the active ingredient in certain approved prescription medicines, including Ozempic and Wegovy, although indications and formulations differ between products and countries.

The existence of approved GLP-1 SMA medicines does not establish that an independently supplied pen is therapeutically equivalent, approved or suitable for clinical administration.

Available GLP-1 SMA Pen Strengths

Specification GLP-1 SMA 10mg GLP-1 SMA 20mg
Total Labelled Content 10mg 20mg
Cartridge Volume 3mL 3mL
Total Volumetric Units 300 300
Format Pre-mixed Pre-mixed
Brand Atlas Longevity Atlas Longevity

The 20mg cartridge contains twice the labelled semaglutide quantity of the 10mg cartridge.

A higher concentration does not mean that a higher amount is medically appropriate.

How Does GLP-1 SMA Work?

GLP-1 SMA activates GLP-1 receptors involved in several metabolic processes.

Its established pharmacological actions include:

  • Stimulating glucose-dependent insulin secretion
  • Reducing inappropriate glucagon secretion
  • Influencing appetite and satiety signalling
  • Delaying gastric emptying
  • Supporting glycaemic control in appropriate clinical settings

The effects, approved uses and treatment outcomes depend on the authorised medicine and prescribed regimen.

GLP-1 SMA and Weight Management

Certain authorised GLP-1 SMA medicines have demonstrated clinically meaningful weight reduction in large human clinical trials.

However, those results apply to the specific studied medicines, doses and treatment conditions.

They should not be used as proof of the safety, effectiveness or equivalence of an unverified pre-mixed GLP-1 SMA pen.

GLP-1 SMA and Type 2 Diabetes

GLP-1 SMA is also used in authorised prescription medicines for glycaemic management in adults with type 2 diabetes.

It is not a substitute for professional diagnosis, medical monitoring or individualised diabetes care.

Understanding the Atlas Pen

The Atlas Pen uses a 3mL cartridge with 300 volumetric units.

Each unit represents 0.01mL of cartridge volume.

The pen dial operates from 1 to 60 units and resets to zero after operation, while remaining cartridge contents stay inside.

These are device specifications, not recommended medical doses.

The concentration, accuracy, sterility and compatibility of any GLP-1 SMA formulation must be independently verified.

Product Quality and Documentation

For any GLP-1 SMA preparation intended for clinical use, relevant quality assurance includes:

  • Verified active ingredient identity
  • Accurate concentration
  • Sterility and microbiological quality
  • Formulation stability
  • Device compatibility and delivery accuracy
  • Appropriate regulatory authorisation

A general peptide purity Certificate of Analysis does not establish that a product is a safe or approved injectable medicine.

Contact Atlas Longevity for available batch-specific documentation.

Storage and Handling

Storage requirements depend on the exact formulation and its validated stability data.

Follow verified product-specific instructions.

Do not assume that storage conditions, shelf life or after-opening periods from Ozempic or Wegovy apply to another GLP-1 SMA formulation.

Important Safety Information

GLP-1 SMA can cause gastrointestinal adverse effects, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation.

More serious risks can include pancreatitis, gallbladder complications, dehydration-related kidney injury and severe gastrointestinal reactions.

Approved GLP-1 SMA medicines also carry important warnings and contraindications that depend on the product and jurisdiction.

Patients using GLP-1 SMA require individual medical assessment, especially when taking other glucose-lowering medications.

GLP-1 SMA should not be used without appropriate medical supervision.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is GLP-1 SMA ?

GLP-1 SMA is a GLP-1 receptor agonist used in certain authorised prescription medicines for metabolic conditions.

What strengths are available?

The Atlas Longevity listing includes 10mg and 20mg pre-mixed pen variations.

What is the difference between the 10mg and 20mg pens?

The 20mg pen contains twice the total labelled GLP-1 SMA quantity of the 10mg pen. Both have a 3mL cartridge.

Is GLP-1 SMA used for weight management?

Yes. Certain authorised GLP-1 SMA medicines are approved for chronic weight management in eligible patients.

Is GLP-1 SMA used for type 2 diabetes?

Yes. Certain authorised GLP-1 SMA medicines are prescribed to improve glycaemic control in people with type 2 diabetes.

How does GLP-1 SMA work?

GLP-1 SMA activates GLP-1 receptors involved in glucose regulation, appetite signalling and gastric emptying.

Does the Atlas GLP-1 SMA Pen require mixing?

The product is presented as a pre-mixed cartridge, without a separate reconstitution step.

How many units are in the pen?

The 3mL Atlas Pen cartridge contains 300 volumetric units, each representing 0.01mL.

BPC-157 Pen

Product Description

BPC-157 is a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide studied primarily for its potential role in tissue repair, vascular signalling, gastrointestinal protection, and inflammatory regulation.

Much of the scientific interest surrounding BPC-157 comes from preclinical research investigating its effects on tendons, ligaments, skeletal muscle, gastrointestinal tissue, nerves, blood vessels, bone, and other connective tissues.

Experimental models have associated BPC-157 with processes including collagen formation, fibroblast activity, angiogenesis, nitric-oxide signalling, and regulation of inflammatory pathways. Pasted text

Atlas Longevity BPC-157 pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click pen system, allowing straightforward concentration and research calculations.

BPC-157 remains an investigational compound and should not be presented as an approved treatment for injury, gastrointestinal disease, inflammation, pain, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

BPC-157 has been investigated extensively in animal and laboratory models, with substantially less human evidence available.

Based on the supplied material:

Evidence Type Status
Human randomized controlled trials Not established
Human observational evidence Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval No

The supplied source specifically characterizes BPC-157 as an experimental research peptide rather than an approved medical therapy. Pasted text

Most of the stronger claims surrounding tissue repair, gastrointestinal protection, nerve regeneration, and musculoskeletal recovery come from animal or cellular studies, so they should not be presented as established human benefits.

Evidence Type

Research described in the supplied material includes:

  • animal tendon and ligament injury models;
  • gastrointestinal ulcer models;
  • skeletal-muscle injury models;
  • peripheral nerve research;
  • vascular injury models;
  • liver-injury research;
  • joint and tendon-to-bone repair studies;
  • cellular and in-vitro investigations;
  • limited observational human information. Pasted text

The quality and clinical relevance of evidence varies considerably between these areas.

Mechanism of Action

BPC-157 appears to influence several biological pathways involved in repair rather than operating through a single established mechanism.

Experimental research has investigated its effects on:

  • angiogenesis, or formation of new blood vessels;
  • VEGF-related signalling;
  • the FAK-paxillin pathway, involved in cellular migration and tissue organization;
  • fibroblast activity;
  • collagen formation and organization;
  • nitric-oxide regulation;
  • inflammatory signalling;
  • endothelial and microvascular function. Pasted text

Together, these pathways may help explain why BPC-157 has attracted attention in tissue-repair and regenerative research.

However, biological mechanisms identified in laboratory or animal models do not establish therapeutic effectiveness in humans.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Tendon, Ligament and Connective-Tissue Research

BPC-157 is frequently investigated in experimental models involving injured tendons, ligaments, and connective tissues.

Animal research described in the supplied material reports changes in fibroblast activity, collagen organization, tendon reattachment, and tissue strength following injury. Pasted text

These findings support continued regenerative research but should not be interpreted as proof that BPC-157 accelerates human injury recovery.

Angiogenesis and Microcirculation

Another major research area involves the formation and stabilization of blood vessels around damaged tissue.

Experimental findings associate BPC-157 with VEGF-related signalling and FAK-paxillin activity, pathways involved in angiogenesis and cellular movement.

This has generated interest in whether the peptide can influence the vascular environment surrounding healing tissues.

Gastrointestinal Research

BPC-157 has been widely investigated in animal models involving:

  • gastric ulcers;
  • intestinal inflammation;
  • mucosal injury;
  • epithelial damage;
  • experimental colitis.

Preclinical research has reported changes in mucosal recovery, epithelial integrity, nitric-oxide signalling, and inflammatory activity. Pasted text

These animal findings do not establish BPC-157 as a proven human treatment for gastrointestinal disease.

Inflammation and Oxidative-Stress Research

BPC-157 research also includes pathways associated with inflammation and oxidative stress.

The supplied material describes experimental changes involving cytokines such as TNF-α and IL-6, nitric-oxide regulation, antioxidant activity, and endothelial function. Pasted text

These findings remain primarily preclinical.

Muscle Repair Research

Animal models of muscle trauma have investigated whether BPC-157 can influence regeneration through vascularisation and repair-related cellular signalling.

Reported findings include increased angiogenesis and changes in muscle-fibre regeneration following experimental injury. Pasted text

Human recovery outcomes have not been established by the supplied evidence.

Nerve and Neurological Research

Preclinical studies have also explored BPC-157 in peripheral nerve and neurological injury models.

Animal findings described in the supplied material include changes in axonal growth, nerve recovery, neuromuscular function, and neurotransmitter-related pathways. Pasted text

This area remains experimental.

Bone and Joint Research

BPC-157 has been investigated in models involving cartilage, bone, joint structures, and tendon-to-bone healing.

Potential mechanisms under investigation include effects on fibroblasts, osteoblasts, chondrocytes, angiogenesis, and growth-factor signalling. Pasted text

Clinical effectiveness for human orthopedic conditions has not been established.

Wound and Skin Repair

Experimental wound models have reported changes in epithelialisation, collagen production, angiogenesis, and wound closure.

These findings have created interest in BPC-157 for broader tissue-regeneration research, although validated human outcomes remain limited. Pasted text

The supplied source discusses experimental combination research involving BPC-157 with several other compounds, including TB-500, GHK-Cu, SS-31, and glutathione. Pasted text

Of these, BPC-157 and TB-500 are discussed around complementary tissue-repair mechanisms involving angiogenesis, fibroblast activity, cellular migration, and cytoskeletal pathways.

However, the supplied material does not establish validated human safety, dosing, compatibility, or efficacy for these combinations.

For that reason, they should be considered research concepts rather than recommended protocols.

MOTS-c 10 mg Pen

Product Description

MOTS-c (Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA type-c) is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA and studied for its role in cellular energy regulation, glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial signalling, and metabolic stress responses.

Unlike most peptides encoded by nuclear DNA, MOTS-c originates from a mitochondrial open reading frame. Research has focused on its ability to act as a metabolic signalling molecule, particularly through pathways associated with AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and cellular responses to energetic stress. Pasted text

Experimental research has examined MOTS-c in relation to:

  • glucose utilisation;
  • insulin signalling;
  • mitochondrial function;
  • fatty-acid metabolism;
  • exercise physiology;
  • oxidative stress;
  • age-associated metabolic changes.

The Atlas Longevity MOTS-c pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

MOTS-c remains under preclinical and early human investigation and should not be presented as an approved treatment for diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome, ageing, fatigue, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The supplied material describes MOTS-c as remaining in preclinical and early human investigation, despite research spanning several experimental models. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human clinical research Early / limited
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

The source labels some evidence as human RCT-level research, but the supporting references provided are dominated by animal studies and reviews.

For Atlas content, the safer characterization is therefore early human plus substantial preclinical research rather than established clinical efficacy.

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • observational research in older adults;
  • diet-induced obesity animal models;
  • exercise physiology research;
  • cellular oxidative-stress models;
  • high-fat-diet mouse studies;
  • cultured myocyte research;
  • an early human pilot study referenced by the source;
  • aged-animal longevity research. Pasted text

Results from animal or cellular research should not automatically be treated as established human metabolic outcomes.

Mechanism of Action

MOTS-c is studied as a mitochondrial-derived metabolic signalling peptide.

Under metabolic stress, the supplied material describes MOTS-c as interacting with both mitochondrial and nuclear signalling pathways.

Research mechanisms include:

  • activation of AMPK;
  • interaction with SIRT1;
  • increased PGC-1α-related activity;
  • regulation of GLUT4-associated glucose transport;
  • modulation of fatty-acid metabolism;
  • influence on mitochondrial biogenesis;
  • changes in oxidative-stress pathways;
  • AKT-associated insulin signalling;
  • interaction with mTORC1-related energy balance. Pasted text

The source also describes movement of MOTS-c into the nucleus during metabolic stress, where it may influence gene-expression responses associated with cellular adaptation.

These findings provide a mechanistic basis for research into metabolism and mitochondrial biology but do not establish therapeutic effectiveness.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

AMPK and Cellular Energy Research

One of the central areas of MOTS-c research involves AMPK, an important cellular energy-sensing pathway.

AMPK responds to changes in cellular energy availability and influences:

  • glucose uptake;
  • fatty-acid oxidation;
  • mitochondrial metabolism;
  • energy conservation;
  • cellular adaptation to stress. Pasted text

MOTS-c is therefore particularly relevant to metabolic-regulation research.

Insulin Signalling and Glucose Utilisation

Experimental studies have investigated whether MOTS-c can influence:

  • insulin sensitivity;
  • glucose tolerance;
  • GLUT4-related glucose transport;
  • cellular glucose uptake.

The supplied material reports changes in these pathways in both preclinical and limited human research contexts. Pasted text

This does not establish MOTS-c as an approved treatment for insulin resistance or diabetes.

Lipid Metabolism Research

MOTS-c has also been studied in animal models examining lipid utilisation.

The supplied material describes increased fatty-acid oxidation and reduced fat accumulation in certain high-fat-diet models. Pasted text

Animal body-composition findings should not be translated into guaranteed human fat-loss outcomes.

Mitochondrial Function

Mitochondrial biology is a major focus of MOTS-c research.

Experimental studies investigate:

  • mitochondrial respiration;
  • ATP-associated energy metabolism;
  • mitochondrial biogenesis;
  • oxidative stress;
  • cellular stress tolerance. Pasted text

Descriptions such as “enhanced mitochondrial efficiency” should be treated as mechanistic research rather than guaranteed clinical benefit.

Metabolic Stress and Ageing Research

MOTS-c has been studied in aged-animal models and other systems involving metabolic stress.

Research areas include:

  • age-associated metabolic decline;
  • high-fat-diet stress;
  • fasting responses;
  • mitochondrial resilience;
  • metabolic homeostasis. Pasted text

These findings make MOTS-c relevant to ageing research, but they do not establish that supplementation slows or reverses human ageing.

  • exercise capacity;
  • skeletal-muscle metabolism;
  • substrate utilisation;
  • mitochondrial gene expression;
  • endurance-related markers. Pasted text

  • DNA-protection mechanisms. Pasted text

These pathways are relevant to cellular stress biology but should not be framed as established disease-prevention effects.

  • CRP-related inflammatory pathways. Pasted text

This does not establish MOTS-c as an approved anti-inflammatory treatment.

  • lifespan-related animal studies. Pasted text

tabs.html:
Tesamorelin 10 mg / 20 mg Pen

Product Description

Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) studied for its ability to stimulate endogenous growth hormone secretion through the pituitary gland.

Rather than supplying growth hormone directly, Tesamorelin activates the body’s GHRH receptor pathway, increasing pulsatile growth hormone signalling and subsequently influencing circulating IGF-1. Clinical research has focused particularly on visceral adipose tissue, metabolic function, lipid biology, liver-related outcomes, and the broader GH–IGF-1 axis. Pasted markdown

Atlas Longevity Tesamorelin pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click cartridge system and are available in:

  • 10 mg Tesamorelin
  • 20 mg Tesamorelin

Tesamorelin has undergone substantial human clinical investigation and has regulatory approval for a specific HIV-associated lipodystrophy indication. That regulatory history applies to authorized Tesamorelin products and indications and should not automatically be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity pen or of unrelated anti-ageing, body-composition, performance, or longevity uses. Pasted markdown

Clinical / Research Status

Tesamorelin has a considerably stronger clinical evidence base than many experimental peptides.

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory approval Yes, for a specific indication/formulation

The supplied material identifies Tesamorelin as FDA-approved in the context of HIV-associated lipodystrophy, while broader metabolic, neurological, regenerative, and ageing applications remain research areas. Pasted markdown

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • multicentre randomized human studies;
  • HIV-associated visceral-fat research;
  • metabolic and lipid studies;
  • liver-fat research;
  • pituitary-receptor assays;
  • muscle and body-composition research;
  • neurocognitive pilot research;
  • observational studies. Pasted markdown

Evidence strength varies depending on the outcome studied.

The strongest human evidence relates to GH/IGF-1 signalling and visceral adipose tissue in defined clinical populations, while claims involving anti-ageing, performance enhancement, skin rejuvenation, or lifespan extension are substantially less established.

Mechanism of Action

Tesamorelin binds to growth hormone-releasing hormone receptors (GHRHR) located on pituitary somatotroph cells.

According to the supplied material, receptor activation stimulates the:

Gαs → adenylate cyclase → cAMP → PKA pathway

which promotes growth hormone synthesis and pulsatile secretion.

The resulting increase in circulating GH can then stimulate hepatic production of IGF-1, which participates in downstream pathways involving:

  • PI3K-Akt;
  • mTOR;
  • JAK-STAT;
  • protein metabolism;
  • lipolysis;
  • tissue signalling. Pasted markdown

GHRH Analogue Activity

Tesamorelin acts upstream at the pituitary gland rather than supplying exogenous growth hormone directly.

The source describes this as allowing endogenous GH feedback mechanisms and pulsatile signalling to remain involved.

Structural Modification

The supplied material describes an N-terminal structural modification intended to increase resistance to DPP-IV degradation, giving Tesamorelin greater stability than native GHRH. Pasted markdown

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Endogenous Growth Hormone Research

Tesamorelin is primarily studied as a GHRH receptor agonist capable of increasing endogenous GH release.

This subsequently influences circulating IGF-1 and provides a model for investigating the physiological GH axis without directly administering growth hormone. Pasted markdown

Visceral Adipose Tissue Research

One of the best-documented research areas for Tesamorelin is visceral adipose tissue (VAT).

Human clinical research described in the supplied material reports reductions in abdominal visceral fat in defined study populations while generally preserving lean tissue. Pasted markdown

This evidence should not be generalized into guaranteed weight-loss or cosmetic body-recomposition outcomes for other populations.

Lipid and Metabolic Research

Tesamorelin has also been investigated for effects involving:

  • triglycerides;
  • cholesterol-related markers;
  • insulin sensitivity;
  • glucose metabolism;
  • broader cardiometabolic endpoints. Pasted markdown

Results vary by population and study design.

Muscle and Recovery Research

The GH–IGF-1 axis plays an important role in protein metabolism and tissue signalling.

The source therefore discusses Tesamorelin in experimental research involving:

  • protein synthesis;
  • muscle-related signalling;
  • satellite-cell activity;
  • recovery physiology. Pasted markdown

This does not establish Tesamorelin as an approved muscle-building or athletic-performance treatment.

Liver and Hepatic-Fat Research

Tesamorelin has been investigated in human research involving hepatic fat and metabolic liver outcomes, particularly in defined HIV populations.

The source discusses changes involving:

  • hepatic steatosis;
  • lipid metabolism;
  • liver-related biomarkers. Pasted markdown

These findings should not be interpreted as broad approval for fatty-liver disease treatment outside studied populations.

Neurocognitive Research

The source also describes emerging research into the relationship between the GH–IGF-1 axis and neurological function.

Experimental areas include:

  • memory;
  • neuronal survival;
  • synaptic plasticity;
  • brain glucose metabolism;
  • neuroendocrine signalling. Pasted markdown

Evidence here is much less established than the visceral-fat clinical literature.

Physiological GH Pulsatility Research

Because Tesamorelin stimulates pituitary GH secretion, research can examine GH signalling while preserving more of the body’s endogenous regulatory architecture than direct GH administration.

The source describes this in relation to:

  • pulsatile secretion;
  • hypothalamic-pituitary feedback;
  • circadian endocrine signalling. Pasted markdown

Collagen and Skin Biology

The supplied material also discusses collagen synthesis and skin-related research through GH/IGF-1 signalling. Pasted markdown

Claims involving younger-looking skin, wound healing, or aesthetic rejuvenation should remain experimental unless supported by formulation-specific clinical evidence.

Physical-Performance Research

Tesamorelin has been discussed in research involving:

  • muscle metabolism;
  • energy utilisation;
  • physical function;
  • endurance-related endpoints. Pasted markdown

The supplied evidence does not establish Tesamorelin as an approved performance-enhancing treatment.

Ageing and Longevity Research

GH and IGF-1 pathways are deeply involved in ageing biology.

The supplied source discusses Tesamorelin in relation to:

  • cellular repair;
  • protein turnover;
  • oxidative stress;
  • metabolic ageing;
  • neuroprotection. Pasted markdown

These are research areas rather than proof that Tesamorelin slows or reverses human ageing.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Human RCTs in HIV-associated lipodystrophy Reduced visceral adipose tissue with increased IGF-1
Human metabolic studies Changes in triglyceride, LDL and insulin-related measures
Rodent metabolic models Increased lipolysis and reduced adipocyte size
In-vitro pituitary assays Increased GH secretion through GHRH/cAMP signalling
Comparative GH research Preservation of physiological GH pulsatility reported by source
Muscle-regeneration models Changes in protein synthesis and satellite-cell-related signalling
Neurocognitive pilot research Changes in memory-related outcomes and GH–IGF-1 signalling

The supplied source reports a 15–20% visceral-fat reduction and approximately 1.7-fold IGF-1 increase after 26 weeks in selected human trial populations. Those figures should be understood as study-specific results, not guaranteed outcomes for other populations or formulations. Pasted markdown

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving Tesamorelin with:

  • CJC-1295 (No-DAC);
  • Ipamorelin;
  • AOD-9604;
  • 5-Amino-1MQ. Pasted markdown

The theoretical rationale involves combining GH-secretagogue, metabolic, or body-composition pathways.

However, the supplied material does not establish validated human safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

Combining multiple GH-axis compounds could also produce overlapping biological effects.

Atlas Longevity therefore does not present these as recommended stacks.

Because Tesamorelin activates the GH–IGF-1 axis, its adverse-effect profile may involve endocrine, metabolic, fluid-balance, and musculoskeletal effects.

What is Tesamorelin?

Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH).

Growth hormone subsequently stimulates hepatic production of IGF-1. Pasted markdown

Dual Growth Hormone Signalling Research Blend

The Atlas Longevity Tesamorelin 20mg + Ipamorelin 10mg Blend combines two peptides associated with distinct pathways involved in growth hormone regulation.

Tesamorelin acts through the GHRH receptor, while Ipamorelin acts through the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a).

The two pathways are relevant to endocrine research, although the safety and effectiveness of this specific combination have not been established through adequate human clinical trials.

What’s Inside the 30mg Blend?

What Is Tesamorelin?

Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone.

It stimulates GHRH receptors in the pituitary gland, which can increase endogenous growth hormone secretion and downstream IGF-1 activity.

Research involving Tesamorelin has examined:

  • Growth hormone secretion
  • Pituitary endocrine signalling
  • IGF-1 regulation
  • Visceral adipose tissue
  • Metabolic pathways
  • Body composition in specific clinical populations

An authorised Tesamorelin medicine is used in certain jurisdictions to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

That approval does not extend to this Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin blend or establish that the blend is suitable for general weight loss.

What Is Ipamorelin?

Ipamorelin is an experimental peptide classified as a growth hormone secretagogue.

It acts primarily through the GHS-R1a receptor, which is also associated with ghrelin signalling.

Research has investigated Ipamorelin in relation to:

  • Growth hormone secretagogue activity
  • Pituitary signalling
  • Ghrelin receptor activation
  • Endocrine regulation
  • Growth hormone release mechanisms

Ipamorelin is not an established approved treatment for muscle growth, fat loss, recovery or anti-ageing.

Why Are Tesamorelin and Ipamorelin Studied Together?

Tesamorelin and Ipamorelin interact with different receptors associated with growth hormone regulation.

Tesamorelin: GHRH receptor pathway.

Ipamorelin: GHS-R1a receptor pathway.

These distinct mechanisms make the combination relevant to experimental endocrine research.

However, combining the two peptides does not establish enhanced effectiveness, improved safety or additional clinical benefits.

CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin Pen

Product Description

CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin is a research peptide combination designed to investigate two complementary pathways involved in pulsatile growth hormone signalling.

CJC-1295 (No-DAC) acts as a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), while Ipamorelin acts primarily through the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a), commonly associated with ghrelin signalling.

By targeting different receptors involved in growth hormone release, the combination is studied for its potential to influence the amplitude and pattern of endogenous GH secretion rather than supplying exogenous growth hormone directly. Pasted text

Research interest includes the GH/IGF-1 axis, recovery biology, body-composition signalling, collagen synthesis, connective-tissue biology, and metabolic regulation.

Atlas Longevity CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin pens use the standard 3 mL cartridge / 300-click system and are available in two strengths:

  • 5 mg CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + 5 mg Ipamorelin
  • 5 mg CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + 10 mg Ipamorelin

These compounds remain investigational and are not established as approved therapeutic treatments.

Clinical / Research Status

The supplied reference describes both CJC-1295-related and Ipamorelin research spanning human, animal, observational, and laboratory evidence.

However, the strength of evidence is not equal across all proposed uses, and the supplied information does not establish regulatory approval for this combination as a therapeutic treatment. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human clinical research Yes
Observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Approved therapeutic use Not established

The reference also lists a regulatory document concerning the combination, but the existence of regulatory documentation should not be confused with therapeutic approval. Pasted text

Evidence Type

The supplied material discusses:

  • human research involving growth-hormone-releasing hormone analogues;
  • human safety research;
  • growth hormone and IGF-1 measurements;
  • animal metabolic models;
  • pituitary-cell research;
  • somatotroph laboratory models;
  • comparative growth hormone secretagogue studies;
  • pharmacodynamic and mechanistic research.

Some cited research concerns the individual components or related CJC-1295 formulations rather than necessarily the exact Atlas CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin combination.

For this reason, findings should be interpreted according to the compound, formulation, and study model actually investigated.

Mechanism of Action

CJC-1295 (No-DAC)

CJC-1295 (No-DAC) is designed to interact with GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotroph cells.

Activation of these receptors can stimulate growth hormone synthesis and release while remaining connected to endogenous hypothalamic-pituitary signalling.

The No-DAC formulation is intended for research into shorter-duration, pulsatile signalling rather than prolonged exposure.

Ipamorelin

Ipamorelin is a selective growth hormone secretagogue that acts primarily through the GHS-R1a receptor.

Activation of this receptor can stimulate intracellular signalling that promotes growth hormone release.

The supplied material describes Ipamorelin as being studied for relatively selective GH stimulation compared with secretagogues that can have broader endocrine effects. Pasted text

Dual-Pathway Research

When the two compounds are investigated together, the scientific rationale is that they stimulate growth hormone release through different but complementary receptor systems.

Researchers therefore examine whether simultaneous GHRH-receptor and GHS-R1a signalling can influence GH pulse amplitude, downstream IGF-1 signalling, metabolism, and regenerative pathways.

This mechanism does not establish guaranteed clinical effects in humans.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Growth Hormone Pulsatility Research

One of the principal areas of interest is the combination’s influence on endogenous growth hormone secretion.

Rather than acting as growth hormone itself, the compounds are studied as signalling molecules that may influence the body’s own GH-release pathways.

The supplied source describes increased GH signalling and downstream IGF-1 activity as central areas of investigation. Pasted text

Muscle Recovery Research

The GH/IGF-1 system participates in protein metabolism, tissue repair, and skeletal-muscle biology.

Experimental research involving growth hormone secretagogues has therefore examined markers related to:

  • muscle-fibre repair;
  • protein synthesis;
  • nitrogen metabolism;
  • satellite-cell activity;
  • recovery following physical stress.

The supplied source discusses these mechanisms, but they should not be interpreted as proof of predictable muscle gain in humans. Pasted text

Metabolic and Adipose-Tissue Research

Growth hormone signalling can influence lipid mobilisation and energy metabolism.

For this reason, CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin research includes investigation of:

  • lipolysis;
  • fatty-acid mobilisation;
  • adipose-tissue metabolism;
  • body-composition signalling;
  • metabolic fuel utilisation. Pasted text

These mechanisms do not establish the combination as an approved weight-loss treatment.

Collagen and Connective-Tissue Research

The GH/IGF-1 pathway is involved in collagen metabolism and connective-tissue biology.

Research interest therefore includes potential effects on:

  • collagen production;
  • tendon and ligament biology;
  • skin extracellular matrix;
  • connective-tissue recovery;
  • musculoskeletal regeneration.

The supplied reference discusses collagen and tissue-repair effects, although clinical outcomes for specific injuries are not established. Pasted text

Bone Metabolism Research

Growth hormone and IGF-1 signalling interact with bone remodelling and osteoblast activity.

The combination is therefore of experimental interest in studies examining bone metabolism, mineralisation, and age-related changes in musculoskeletal biology.

This research area should not be interpreted as evidence that the combination treats osteoporosis or other bone disorders.

Sleep and Circadian GH Research

Growth hormone secretion naturally follows a pulsatile pattern, with substantial secretion associated with sleep.

The supplied source discusses the combination in relation to nocturnal GH secretion and sleep-associated recovery processes. Pasted text

However, the evidence supplied is not sufficient to present improved sleep quality as a guaranteed clinical benefit.

Regenerative and Recovery Research

Growth hormone and IGF-1 participate in multiple pathways related to cellular repair.

Researchers therefore investigate GH secretagogues in models involving:

  • muscle recovery;
  • collagen synthesis;
  • tissue remodelling;
  • physical stress;
  • connective-tissue repair.

Human therapeutic recovery claims cannot be established from these mechanisms alone.

Endocrine Rhythm Research

The No-DAC formulation is of particular interest in research focused on pulsatile rather than continuously elevated GH signalling.

This makes the combination relevant to studies examining the timing, amplitude, and physiological pattern of pituitary growth hormone release.

The supplied reference discusses experimental research concepts combining CJC-1295 (No-DAC) + Ipamorelin with:

  • GHK-Cu;

tabs.html:
Melanotan II 10 mg Pen

Product Description

Melanotan II (MT-II) is a synthetic cyclic analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) studied for its effects on melanocortin receptors, melanogenesis, pigmentation, appetite-related signalling, sexual-function pathways, and neuroendocrine regulation.

Unlike more selective melanocortin analogues, Melanotan II can interact with multiple melanocortin receptor subtypes. Its activity at MC1R is associated with melanin production, while central activity involving MC3R and MC4R has generated research interest in appetite, energy balance, and sexual-arousal pathways. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity Melanotan II pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Melanotan II remains an unapproved investigational peptide. It should not be presented as an approved treatment for tanning, obesity, sexual dysfunction, metabolic disorders, photoprotection, or other medical conditions. Pasted text

Clinical / Research Status

Melanotan II has been investigated in human, animal, observational, and laboratory research.

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval No

The supplied material specifically states that Melanotan II remains a research peptide and is not approved for therapeutic use. Pasted text

Human research demonstrating biological activity should therefore not be interpreted as evidence of approved or established medical use.

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • early human pigmentation studies;
  • observational sexual-response research;
  • rodent hypothalamic models;
  • melanocyte cultures;
  • metabolic animal research;
  • pharmacokinetic studies;
  • behavioural neurobiology models. Pasted text

The strength of evidence differs considerably depending on the proposed effect.

Pigmentation and melanocortin-receptor activity have more direct experimental support than broad claims involving mood, longevity, systemic recovery, or anti-ageing.

Mechanism of Action

Melanotan II interacts with several members of the melanocortin receptor family.

MC1R and Pigmentation

Activation of MC1R on melanocytes stimulates intracellular cAMP signalling and increases activity of enzymes involved in melanin production, including tyrosinase.

This can increase melanogenesis and skin pigmentation in experimental models.

MC3R and MC4R Signalling

Melanotan II also interacts with central melanocortin receptors, particularly MC3R and MC4R.

These receptors participate in pathways associated with:

  • appetite;
  • energy balance;
  • sexual arousal;
  • neuroendocrine signalling.

The cyclic structure of Melanotan II contributes to greater stability and receptor activity compared with endogenous α-MSH. Pasted text

Because Melanotan II is not highly selective for one receptor, its biological effects can extend beyond pigmentation.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Melanogenesis and Pigmentation Research

The primary research use of Melanotan II involves MC1R activation and melanin synthesis.

Experimental studies have reported increased melanocyte activity and pigmentation following exposure to Melanotan II. Pasted text

This does not establish Melanotan II as an approved cosmetic tanning product.

UV-Response and Photobiology Research

Melanin participates in the skin’s natural response to ultraviolet radiation.

Increased eumelanin production has therefore generated research interest in:

  • UV-response biology;
  • oxidative skin stress;
  • pigmentation adaptation;
  • photoprotection mechanisms. Pasted text

Melanotan II should not be represented as a substitute for sunscreen, protective clothing, or established UV-protection measures.

Appetite and Energy-Balance Research

MC4R is an important regulator of appetite and energy homeostasis.

Preclinical Melanotan II research has reported changes in:

  • food intake;
  • body weight;
  • energy expenditure;
  • lipid metabolism. Pasted text

These findings do not establish Melanotan II as an approved weight-loss treatment.

Sexual-Function Research

Central melanocortin signalling is involved in sexual arousal and erectile physiology.

Melanotan II has been investigated experimentally for its effects on:

  • sexual arousal;
  • erectile responses;
  • libido-related pathways;
  • reproductive behaviour. Pasted text

This activity is biologically meaningful but also contributes to potential adverse effects such as prolonged erections.

Neuroendocrine Research

Because Melanotan II interacts with central melanocortin receptors, it is also studied in neuroendocrine and behavioural models.

The supplied material discusses possible effects involving dopaminergic, serotonergic, reward, motivation, and emotional pathways. Pasted text

These areas should be described cautiously because the evidence does not establish Melanotan II as a treatment for mood or neurological disorders.

Inflammatory and Oxidative-Stress Research

The supplied source also describes experimental research involving melanocortin signalling and:

  • inflammatory cytokines;
  • TNF-α;
  • IL-1β;
  • reactive oxygen species;
  • antioxidant activity. Pasted text

These findings remain primarily mechanistic or preclinical.

Metabolic Research

Melanotan II’s effects on hypothalamic melanocortin pathways have made it useful in experimental metabolic research.

Areas investigated include:

  • appetite regulation;
  • glucose handling;
  • insulin-related pathways;
  • lipid oxidation;
  • energy expenditure. Pasted text

These effects should not be translated into guaranteed fat-loss or metabolic benefits in humans.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Early human clinical research Increased skin pigmentation intensity and duration
Human observational research Changes in erectile response and libido-related signalling
Rodent hypothalamic models Reduced food intake and body weight through central melanocortin pathways
In-vitro melanocyte cultures Increased tyrosinase activity and melanin synthesis
Rat metabolic studies Increased energy expenditure and lipid-oxidation markers
Pharmacokinetic studies Greater stability and receptor persistence than endogenous α-MSH
Behavioural neurobiology models Changes in central signalling associated with arousal and behaviour

These results span human, animal, and cellular research, so findings from one model should not automatically be generalized to another. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied material discusses experimental combinations involving:

  • Melanotan II + PT-141;
  • Melanotan II + GHK-Cu. Pasted text

Because PT-141 and Melanotan II both interact with melanocortin pathways, combining them could theoretically increase overlapping biological effects as well as adverse effects.

The supplied evidence does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

Atlas Longevity therefore does not present them as recommended stacks.

KPV 10 mg Pen

Product Description

KPV (Lysine-Proline-Valine) is a short tripeptide derived from the C-terminal region of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH). It is studied primarily for its potential role in inflammatory signalling, cytokine regulation, epithelial-barrier biology, and localized immune regulation.

Unlike broader melanocortin compounds, KPV is investigated for anti-inflammatory activity that may occur without activating the full range of melanocortin signalling pathways.

Preclinical research has examined KPV in models involving TNF-α, interleukin signalling, NF-κB activity, intestinal epithelial integrity, inflammatory bowel models, and dermatological inflammation. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity KPV pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

KPV remains an investigational research peptide. It should not be presented as an approved treatment for inflammatory bowel disease, dermatitis, autoimmune disease, chronic inflammation, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The evidence supplied for KPV is predominantly preclinical, with animal and in-vitro studies forming the strongest part of the research base.

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material

Human observational research Limited / indirect
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

The supplied source itself identifies KPV primarily with inflammatory-modulation and epithelial-barrier research. Pasted text

Evidence involving α-MSH or related melanocortin peptides should not automatically be treated as direct clinical evidence for KPV.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • mouse colitis models;
  • nanoparticle-delivered KPV in inflammatory bowel models;
  • murine atopic dermatitis;
  • LPS-stimulated macrophage cultures;
  • keratinocyte and fibroblast assays;
  • allergic contact dermatitis models;
  • intestinal epithelial cell lines. Pasted text

This means most proposed applications should be described as experimental research areas rather than established human benefits.

Mechanism of Action

KPV is studied primarily for its effects on NF-κB-associated inflammatory signalling.

NF-κB is a transcription factor involved in controlling expression of numerous inflammatory genes.

According to the supplied material, experimental KPV activity has been associated with:

  • inhibition of IKK-related activity;
  • reduced IκB degradation;
  • decreased NF-κB nuclear translocation;
  • reduced transcription of TNF-α;
  • changes in IL-6 and other inflammatory mediators;
  • modulation of mast-cell activity. Pasted text

These pathways provide the main mechanistic basis for research into KPV’s potential anti-inflammatory properties.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Inflammatory Signalling Research

KPV is studied for its potential to regulate excessive inflammatory signalling rather than simply suppressing all immune activity.

Experimental models have reported changes in pro-inflammatory mediators such as:

TNF-α, IL-6, NF-κB and related cytokine pathways. Pasted text

This does not establish KPV as a clinically proven anti-inflammatory treatment.

Gut and Epithelial Barrier Research

One of the more prominent areas of KPV research involves intestinal epithelial biology.

Experimental inflammatory bowel models have investigated its potential influence on:

  • epithelial integrity;
  • mucosal recovery;
  • tight-junction proteins;
  • intestinal inflammatory signalling;
  • barrier stability. Pasted text

These findings are primarily preclinical.

Cytokine Regulation Research

Cytokines coordinate communication between immune cells.

Excessive cytokine signalling can contribute to persistent inflammatory processes.

KPV has therefore been investigated for its ability to modify the intensity of certain inflammatory signals rather than completely eliminating normal immune communication. Pasted text

Skin Inflammation Research

KPV has also been investigated in experimental dermatological models.

Research involving keratinocytes and animal skin models has examined changes in:

  • inflammatory-marker expression;
  • mast-cell activity;
  • edema;
  • leukocyte infiltration;
  • wound-associated signalling. Pasted text

Evidence from these models should not be presented as proof that injectable KPV treats human dermatological conditions.

Immune-Regulation Research

A central research concept surrounding KPV is immune modulation rather than broad immune suppression.

Its relatively small structure and focused signalling profile make it relevant to experimental models examining localized inflammatory regulation. Pasted text

The clinical significance of this selectivity remains uncertain.

Chronic Low-Grade Inflammation Research

KPV has also been investigated in experimental systems designed to model prolonged inflammatory stress.

These models are relevant to research examining how persistent inflammatory signalling affects epithelial barriers, metabolism, and tissue integrity. Pasted text

This does not establish KPV as a treatment for systemic or chronic inflammatory disease.

tabs.html:
Cagrilintide is a synthetic long-acting analogue of amylin, a hormone normally co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic beta cells.

Amylin participates in the regulation of satiety, meal size, gastric emptying, postprandial glucose handling, and energy intake. Cagrilintide has been structurally modified to provide substantially longer biological activity than native amylin, allowing sustained investigation of amylin-receptor signalling.

Human clinical research has examined Cagrilintide in relation to:

  • appetite regulation;
  • reduced energy intake;
  • body-weight change;
  • obesity research;
  • gastric-emptying physiology;
  • metabolic regulation;
  • combination incretin-based research.

The Atlas Longevity Cagrilintide pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Cagrilintide remains an investigational metabolic compound within the material supplied. Human clinical evidence exists, but the source does not establish general regulatory approval for the Atlas Longevity formulation or for routine weight-management treatment.

Clinical / Research Status

Cagrilintide has progressed into substantial human clinical investigation, particularly in overweight, obesity, and metabolic research.

The source describes multiple human studies examining Cagrilintide alone and in combination with GLP-1-related compounds.

Human research provides more direct evidence than exists for many experimental peptides, but findings remain formulation-, population-, and protocol-specific.

Evidence Type

The supplied material describes research involving:

  • Phase 1b studies in adults with overweight or obesity;
  • human satiety studies;
  • metabolic profiling;
  • combination research with GLP-1 SMA;
  • diet-induced obesity animal models;
  • amylin-receptor binding assays.

The strongest source-supported areas are appetite regulation, satiety, food-intake reduction, and body-weight research.

Claims involving broader metabolic optimisation should remain secondary to those established research domains.

Mechanism of Action

Cagrilintide acts primarily as a long-acting amylin receptor agonist.

Amylin receptors are not single standalone receptors. They are formed from combinations of:

  • the calcitonin receptor;
  • receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMPs).

These receptor complexes are expressed in areas of the nervous system involved in appetite and satiety regulation.

Central Satiety Signalling

Cagrilintide activates amylin-sensitive signalling in brain regions including the:

  • area postrema;
  • brainstem;
  • hypothalamic appetite-control networks.

These regions integrate circulating nutrient-related signals and contribute to:

  • meal termination;
  • fullness;
  • hunger regulation;
  • energy intake.

Gastric Emptying

Amylin signalling also influences gastrointestinal motility.

Slower gastric emptying can alter:

  • nutrient delivery;
  • post-meal glucose appearance;
  • duration of fullness;
  • postprandial satiety.

Long-Acting Design

Native amylin is cleared relatively quickly.

Cagrilintide has been engineered for prolonged activity, allowing substantially more sustained receptor engagement and making it useful in longer-duration metabolic research.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Satiety and Appetite Research

Cagrilintide is primarily investigated for its influence on physiological satiety pathways rather than stimulant-style appetite suppression.

Activation of amylin receptors influences central circuits involved in:

  • hunger;
  • fullness;
  • meal size;
  • food-seeking behaviour.

This is one of the principal mechanistic foundations of Cagrilintide research.

Energy-Intake Research

Human studies have examined whether sustained amylin signalling can reduce overall energy intake.

The mechanism appears to act upstream by altering appetite and meal-related signalling rather than directly increasing metabolic rate.

Body-Weight Research

Clinical research has examined Cagrilintide in adults with overweight or obesity.

The supplied source reports body-weight reductions in selected controlled studies, including substantial changes over multi-month research periods.

These study-specific findings should not be interpreted as guaranteed results for every population or formulation.

Gastric-Emptying Research

Cagrilintide is also relevant to research involving:

  • delayed gastric emptying;
  • prolonged postprandial fullness;
  • nutrient-delivery kinetics;
  • post-meal metabolic responses.

This peripheral mechanism complements its central satiety activity.

Postprandial Metabolic Research

Amylin is naturally co-secreted with insulin.

Research therefore examines how Cagrilintide-related amylin signalling interacts with:

  • nutrient processing;
  • postprandial glucose regulation;
  • pancreatic signalling;
  • energy homeostasis.

Amylin Receptor Biology

Cagrilintide provides a model for investigating signalling through calcitonin receptor/RAMP complexes.

This includes research into:

  • receptor specificity;
  • ligand binding;
  • sustained receptor activation;
  • neural appetite circuitry.

Combination Incretin Research

A major area of interest involves combining amylin signalling with incretin pathways.

GLP-1 receptor agonism and amylin receptor agonism influence energy intake through overlapping but distinct mechanisms.

The supplied source specifically discusses combination research with GLP-1 SMA, including the investigational CagriSema concept.

The supplied material discusses experimental combinations involving:

  • Cagrilintide + GLP-1 SMA;

The strongest clinical rationale among those listed relates to Cagrilintide + GLP-1 SMA, because this combination has been directly investigated in human clinical research.

The other combinations should be treated more cautiously.

Combining Cagrilintide with incretin-based compounds could produce overlapping effects involving:

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Cagrilintide?

Cagrilintide is a synthetic long-acting amylin analogue investigated mainly for appetite regulation, satiety, energy-intake reduction, body-weight research, and metabolic signalling.

What is amylin?

Amylin is a hormone normally co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic beta cells.

It contributes to:

  • satiety;
  • meal-size regulation;
  • gastric emptying;
  • postprandial metabolic control.

How does Cagrilintide work?

Cagrilintide activates amylin receptor complexes in central nervous system regions involved in satiety and appetite regulation.

It also influences gastric emptying, which can prolong fullness and alter post-meal nutrient delivery.

Where are amylin receptors located?

Important sites include the area postrema and hypothalamic appetite-regulation pathways.

These regions help integrate circulating nutrient signals with central hunger and satiety responses.

What are RAMPs?

RAMPs are receptor activity-modifying proteins.

Amylin receptors are formed when calcitonin receptors associate with particular RAMP proteins.

These combinations alter receptor pharmacology and ligand specificity.

Is Cagrilintide a GLP-1 receptor agonist?

No.

Cagrilintide is primarily an amylin analogue, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

However, amylin and GLP-1 pathways can influence overlapping aspects of appetite and energy regulation.

Is Cagrilintide the same as GLP-1 SMA?

No.

Cagrilintide primarily targets amylin receptor systems, while GLP-1 SMA acts through the GLP-1 receptor.

The two have been investigated together because they affect energy balance through distinct but complementary pathways.

What is CagriSema?

The supplied material uses CagriSema to describe research involving Cagrilintide together with GLP-1 SMA.

Combination-study findings should not automatically be applied to Cagrilintide alone.

What is Cagrilintide researched for?

Major research areas include:

  • satiety;
  • appetite;
  • energy intake;
  • body weight;
  • obesity;
  • gastric emptying;
  • glucose-related metabolism;
  • combination incretin research.

Has Cagrilintide been studied in humans?

The supplied material describes multiple controlled human trials involving overweight, obesity, metabolic regulation, and combination therapy.

Does Cagrilintide reduce body weight?

Human clinical research described in the source reports body-weight reductions in selected study populations.

Those results are specific to particular trial designs, doses, durations, and populations and should not be treated as guaranteed outcomes.

Does Cagrilintide slow gastric emptying?

Amylin receptor activation can slow gastric emptying.

The supplied source discusses delayed gastric emptying and prolonged postprandial fullness as part of Cagrilintide’s research profile.

Does Cagrilintide suppress appetite?

Appetite and satiety regulation are major research endpoints for Cagrilintide.

Its mechanism involves physiological satiety pathways rather than stimulant-mediated appetite suppression.

tabs.title: Description
tabs.html:
CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic long-acting analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to produce sustained stimulation of the growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) axis.

The peptide contains a Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) modification that enables prolonged association with circulating albumin. This substantially extends its biological persistence compared with native GHRH and shorter-acting GHRH analogues.

Research has examined CJC-1295 with DAC in relation to:

  • endogenous growth hormone secretion;
  • circulating IGF-1;
  • pituitary GHRH receptor signalling;
  • GH pulse amplitude;
  • metabolic regulation;
  • body-composition biology;
  • tissue-repair signalling;
  • prolonged somatotropic-axis activation.

The Atlas Longevity CJC-1295 with DAC pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

CJC-1295 with DAC remains an investigational research peptide. The supplied material describes early human pharmacokinetic research alongside animal and in-vitro evidence, but it is not presented as an approved medicine.

Clinical / Research Status

The supplied material describes CJC-1295 with DAC as having undergone limited early-phase human investigation, particularly in pharmacokinetic and GH/IGF-1 research.

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized clinical research Not established by supplied status section
Human observational / early-phase research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory approval No

The source’s evidence table marks human RCT evidence as absent while some later references are labelled as human RCTs. For Atlas content, the more cautious description is therefore limited human pharmacokinetic and endocrine research rather than a broad established clinical evidence base.

Evidence Type

The supplied material describes research involving:

  • healthy adult human pharmacokinetic studies;
  • repeated human exposure studies;
  • pituitary-cell research;
  • GHRH receptor assays;
  • aged-animal models;
  • growth-hormone-deficient animal models.

The strongest source-supported findings concern prolonged GH and IGF-1 elevation following CJC-1295 with DAC exposure.

Claims involving muscle gain, fat loss, sleep, skin rejuvenation, bone density, or anti-ageing should remain secondary and research-oriented.

Mechanism of Action

CJC-1295 with DAC acts as a GHRH receptor agonist.

It binds to GHRH receptors on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells, stimulating endogenous growth hormone secretion.

The resulting increase in GH can subsequently increase production of:

IGF-1

primarily through hepatic GH signalling.

GHRH Receptor Activation

Activation of the GHRH receptor stimulates intracellular signalling associated with:

  • adenylate cyclase;
  • cAMP;
  • protein kinase A;
  • GH synthesis;
  • GH secretion.

Drug Affinity Complex (DAC)

The defining feature of CJC-1295 with DAC is its albumin-binding DAC modification.

The source describes this as allowing prolonged association with serum albumin, substantially slowing peptide clearance.

This is the basis for the source-reported half-life of approximately:

6–8 days

compared with the much shorter persistence of native GHRH.

Sustained GH / IGF-1 Signalling

Because the compound remains biologically available for longer, experimental exposure can produce more prolonged changes in:

  • mean GH concentration;
  • GH pulse amplitude;
  • IGF-1 levels.

The supplied material specifically describes sustained increases rather than complete replacement of physiological GH pulsatility.

CJC-1295 with DAC vs CJC-1295 No-DAC

The two compounds should not be treated as interchangeable.

CJC-1295 with DAC

Designed for long-duration systemic exposure through albumin binding.

Source-reported half-life:

approximately 6–8 days

CJC-1295 No-DAC

A much shorter-acting GHRH analogue without the albumin-binding DAC modification.

Its pharmacokinetic behaviour and research design are therefore substantially different.

Any click calculations, timing concepts, or research interpretation should be kept specific to the exact CJC-1295 variant being discussed.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Sustained Growth Hormone Research

The main research characteristic of CJC-1295 with DAC is its ability to produce prolonged stimulation of endogenous GH secretion.

Human research described by the source reports elevated mean GH concentrations for several days following exposure.

This makes CJC-1295 with DAC useful in models examining chronic rather than brief GHRH receptor stimulation.

IGF-1 Research

Increased GH signalling can raise circulating IGF-1.

The source reports prolonged IGF-1 elevations following CJC-1295 with DAC administration, extending beyond the initial GH response.

This is one of the most clearly described downstream endpoints in the supplied material.

GH Pulsatility Research

The source states that CJC-1295 with DAC can increase GH pulse amplitude while preserving endogenous pulsatile characteristics.

This makes the compound relevant to research into:

  • somatotropic-axis physiology;
  • GH pulse architecture;
  • long-duration GHRH stimulation.

Body-Composition Research

Because the GH/IGF-1 axis influences protein and lipid metabolism, CJC-1295 with DAC has been studied in experimental models involving:

  • lean tissue;
  • adipose tissue;
  • protein metabolism;
  • body composition.

Most claims involving significant muscle gain or fat loss remain more preclinical than established human outcomes.

Lipolysis Research

Growth hormone participates in adipose-tissue metabolism and lipolytic signalling.

The supplied source discusses experimental reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat in selected models.

These findings should not be translated into guaranteed human fat-loss outcomes.

Tissue-Repair Research

The GH–IGF-1 axis participates in:

  • fibroblast signalling;
  • collagen synthesis;
  • satellite-cell biology;
  • connective-tissue turnover.

CJC-1295 with DAC is therefore discussed in experimental tissue-repair and recovery research.

This does not establish the compound as an approved treatment for injury or musculoskeletal repair.

Sleep and GH-Release Research

Growth hormone secretion is physiologically associated with sleep, particularly slow-wave sleep.

The supplied source discusses CJC-1295 with DAC in relation to sleep architecture and nocturnal GH signalling.

However, evidence for direct sleep improvement is weaker than the pharmacokinetic evidence for GH and IGF-1 elevation.

Bone and Skeletal Research

GH and IGF-1 influence bone remodelling.

Experimental research described by the source discusses:

  • osteoblast activity;
  • collagen type I;
  • mineralisation;
  • skeletal remodelling.

These findings remain research-oriented and should not be presented as proof of improved human bone density.

Skin and Collagen Research

The source also discusses experimental effects on dermal collagen and extracellular-matrix biology.

This provides a mechanistic basis for skin-related research but does not establish anti-ageing or cosmetic rejuvenation outcomes.

Metabolic Research

Sustained GH elevation can influence:

  • glucose metabolism;
  • insulin sensitivity;
  • lipid metabolism;
  • substrate utilisation.

These effects can be complex and may include reduced insulin sensitivity rather than uniformly beneficial metabolic changes.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Healthy adult human PK study Mean plasma GH reportedly increased approximately 2–10 fold for several days, with IGF-1 elevated for longer
Repeated human exposure Sustained IGF-1 elevation across repeated exposure periods
Human pharmacokinetic research Source-reported effective half-life approximately 5.8–8.1 days
Rat pituitary-cell cultures GHRH receptor activation with preserved pulsatile GH release
Aged rodent models Increased GH pulse amplitude with body-composition changes
GH-deficient animal models Increased IGF-1 and somatic-growth-related markers
In-vitro receptor assays Prolonged GHRH receptor engagement relative to native GHRH

The strongest conclusions supported by the supplied material concern pharmacokinetics and sustained GH/IGF-1 signalling, while broader body-composition and regenerative claims rely more heavily on preclinical evidence.

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving:

  • CJC-1295 with DAC + Ipamorelin;
  • CJC-1295 with DAC + BPC-157;
  • CJC-1295 with DAC + Tesamorelin;
  • CJC-1295 with DAC + MK-677;
  • CJC-1295 with DAC + Hexarelin.

The proposed rationale is generally to combine sustained GHRH signalling with other:

  • GH secretagogues;
  • ghrelin-receptor agonists;
  • regenerative compounds;
  • metabolic research compounds.

However, combining multiple GH-axis compounds can also produce overlapping endocrine effects.

The supplied material does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

What Is HCG?

Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (HCG) is a naturally occurring glycoprotein hormone involved in reproductive endocrine signalling.

HCG activates the luteinising hormone/chorionic gonadotropin receptor (LHCGR).

In males, this receptor is involved in testosterone production by Leydig cells. In females, it participates in ovarian function and reproductive hormone regulation.

Format Pre-mixed Pre-mixed
Brand Atlas Longevity Atlas Longevity

The two variations contain different labelled quantities of biological activity in the same cartridge volume.

HCG Research Areas

HCG is relevant to scientific and clinical research involving:

  • Reproductive endocrinology
  • Luteinising hormone receptor signalling
  • Leydig cell function
  • Testosterone-associated steroidogenesis
  • Ovarian hormone signalling
  • Fertility-related hormonal pathways

Certain authorised HCG medicines have established clinical applications. This does not establish that an Atlas Longevity pen is an approved medicine.

The Atlas Pen uses a 3mL cartridge containing 300 volumetric units.

Each unit represents 0.01mL of cartridge volume, and the dial operates from 1 to 60 units.

The dial resets to zero after operation, while the remaining cartridge contents stay inside the pen.

These specifications describe the device mechanism and do not constitute medical dosing instructions.

Pre-Mixed Formulation

The pen format alone does not establish suitability for human injection.

Quality Documentation

Storage and Safety

Follow verified formulation-specific storage and expiry instructions.

HCG is a biologically active hormone. Potential adverse effects and contraindications depend on the patient, indication and formulation.

Clinical administration requires a legally authorised medicine and qualified medical supervision.

It is a pre-mixed cartridge pen labelled as containing Human Chorionic Gonadotropin.

The HCG Pen is available in 1,000 IU and 5,000 IU variations.

IU stands for International Unit, a standardised measurement of biological activity.

What is HCG researched for?

HCG is studied in reproductive endocrinology, gonadal signalling and hormone regulation.

Does HCG stimulate testosterone production?

HCG can stimulate testosterone production through LH receptor activation in functioning Leydig cells.

Is HCG used in fertility treatment?

Certain authorised HCG medicines are used in selected fertility treatments under medical supervision.

Is the HCG Pen an approved medicine?

The pen’s regulatory approval status must be verified independently. An HCG product should not be assumed to be authorised simply because HCG is used in approved medicines.

tabs.title: Description
tabs.html:
Somatropin (recombinant human growth hormone / rhGH) is a 191-amino-acid peptide hormone designed to match endogenous human growth hormone produced by the pituitary gland.

Growth hormone plays a central role in growth, metabolism, tissue turnover, protein synthesis, lipid mobilisation, bone biology, and IGF-1 signalling. Somatropin has therefore been extensively investigated in clinical and experimental research involving growth hormone deficiency, body composition, connective tissue, skeletal physiology, and metabolic regulation.

Somatropin acts both directly through the growth hormone receptor (GHR) and indirectly by stimulating production of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1).

Atlas Longevity Somatropin pens are available in:

  • 10 IU HGH Pen
  • 36 IU HGH Pen

Both use the Atlas standard:

3 mL cartridge volume

300 total pen units / clicks

1 click = 0.01 mL

The 10 IU variant replaces the previously referenced 24 IU pen. The 36 IU variant remains available.

Clinical / Research Status

Somatropin has a substantially stronger clinical evidence base than most experimental peptides.

Evidence Type Status
Human randomized clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic use Yes, for specific approved indications

The supplied material describes Somatropin as an FDA-approved growth hormone medication for specific clinical conditions while emphasizing that uses outside approved indications remain investigational.

Approval of specific prescription Somatropin products should not automatically be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity Somatropin pen or of anti-ageing, bodybuilding, performance-enhancement, or cosmetic uses.

Mechanism of Action

Somatropin binds to growth hormone receptors (GHRs) located throughout multiple tissues.

Growth hormone receptor activation initiates intracellular signalling involving:

  • JAK2
  • STAT5
  • MAPK / ERK
  • PI3K / Akt
  • downstream mTOR-related signalling

These pathways influence gene transcription involved in:

  • cellular growth;
  • protein metabolism;
  • tissue differentiation;
  • repair processes;
  • lipid metabolism.

IGF-1 Signalling

A major downstream effect of growth hormone is stimulation of IGF-1 production, particularly in the liver.

IGF-1 contributes to many of the anabolic and growth-related effects associated with the GH axis, including signalling within:

  • skeletal muscle;
  • bone;
  • connective tissue;
  • cartilage;
  • other growth-responsive tissues.

Lipid Metabolism

Growth hormone also influences adipose-tissue metabolism and lipolytic pathways.

These metabolic actions are separate from its growth-promoting effects and are an important area of GH research.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Growth Hormone and IGF-1 Research

Somatropin is one of the principal compounds used to study direct growth hormone receptor activation.

Unlike GHRH analogues or secretagogues, Somatropin provides the growth hormone molecule itself rather than stimulating the pituitary to increase endogenous release.

This makes it useful for research comparing:

  • direct GH exposure;
  • GHRH stimulation;
  • ghrelin-receptor secretagogues;
  • downstream IGF-1 responses.

Protein Synthesis and Lean-Tissue Research

Growth hormone and IGF-1 are involved in protein metabolism.

Research has examined effects involving:

  • amino-acid utilisation;
  • nitrogen retention;
  • protein turnover;
  • lean body mass;
  • skeletal-muscle signalling.

Changes in lean mass do not necessarily translate directly into proportional increases in functional strength or athletic performance.

Adipose-Tissue and Lipolysis Research

Somatropin has also been studied for its ability to influence:

  • fat mobilisation;
  • adipocyte metabolism;
  • visceral adipose tissue;
  • lipid oxidation.

This makes GH important in metabolic and body-composition research.

It should not be presented as an approved general fat-loss treatment.

Bone and Skeletal Research

Growth hormone and IGF-1 influence:

  • osteoblast activity;
  • bone turnover;
  • skeletal growth;
  • collagen synthesis;
  • mineralisation.

Somatropin is therefore widely studied in growth and skeletal biology.

Connective-Tissue and Collagen Research

Experimental studies investigate GH/IGF-1 signalling in relation to:

  • fibroblast activity;
  • collagen production;
  • extracellular matrix turnover;
  • tissue remodelling.

These mechanisms provide a basis for regenerative research but do not establish guaranteed healing effects.

Metabolic Research

Growth hormone has complex effects on glucose and lipid metabolism.

Experimental endpoints include:

  • insulin sensitivity;
  • glucose utilisation;
  • hepatic metabolism;
  • lipid profiles;
  • substrate distribution.

Importantly, increased GH exposure can also reduce insulin sensitivity, so its metabolic effects should not be characterized as universally beneficial.

Neurological and Neuroendocrine Research

GH and IGF-1 signalling also interact with the nervous system.

Research areas include:

  • neuroendocrine regulation;
  • cognition;
  • sleep;
  • brain GH signalling;
  • neuronal IGF-1 pathways.

Evidence for direct cognitive enhancement remains less established than the endocrine and growth-related effects of Somatropin.

Skin and Extracellular-Matrix Research

Somatropin-related studies have also examined:

  • dermal collagen;
  • skin thickness;
  • tissue hydration;
  • extracellular-matrix biology.

These findings should remain framed as research rather than proven cosmetic anti-ageing outcomes.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
GH-deficient adult clinical studies Increased lean body mass and reduced fat mass reported during GH replacement
Older-adult research Changes in skin thickness and collagen-related measurements
Fracture animal models Increased callus formation and osteoblast-related activity
Wound-healing research Increased fibroblast activity and collagen synthesis in experimental systems
Human metabolic studies Changes in lipid metabolism and glucose-related endpoints
Exercise and recovery studies Changes in body composition and recovery-related markers
In-vitro cell research Increased STAT5 signalling and IGF-1 gene expression
Long-term experimental models Sustained effects on protein turnover and metabolic signalling

Clinical outcomes depend strongly on the population studied, underlying GH status, exposure, duration, and formulation.

Somatropin vs GH Secretagogues

Somatropin should be distinguished from compounds such as:

  • CJC-1295;
  • Tesamorelin;
  • Ipamorelin;
  • GHRP-6.

Somatropin

Provides growth hormone directly.

GHRH Analogues

Compounds such as CJC-1295 and Tesamorelin stimulate the pituitary through the GHRH receptor.

Ghrelin-Receptor Secretagogues

Compounds such as Ipamorelin stimulate GH release through the GHS-R1a / ghrelin receptor pathway.

These approaches affect the GH axis differently and should not be treated as interchangeable.

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied material discusses experimental combinations involving Somatropin with:

  • IGF-1 LR3;
  • BPC-157;
  • TB-500;
  • Epitalon;
  • SS-31;
  • NAD+;
  • CJC-1295;
  • Ipamorelin.

These combinations involve overlapping pathways related to growth signalling, regeneration, metabolism, or mitochondrial research.

Combining direct HGH with GH-releasing compounds can also increase overall GH/IGF-1 pathway exposure.

The supplied information does not establish validated safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

Possible Side Effects

Somatropin has a well-characterized physiological effect profile because it directly activates the growth hormone pathway.

The supplied material identifies potential effects including:

  • peripheral edema;
  • fluid retention;

  • arthralgia;
  • carpal-tunnel-type symptoms;
  • headache;

  • insulin resistance;
  • hyperglycaemia;
  • fatigue.

This may contribute to:

  • swelling;
  • edema;
  • soft-tissue fullness;
  • nerve-compression symptoms.

Glucose and Insulin Sensitivity

One of the most important metabolic considerations is that GH can reduce insulin sensitivity.

Prolonged or excessive exposure may therefore influence:

  • fasting glucose;
  • glucose tolerance;
  • insulin resistance.

Carpal-Tunnel-Type Symptoms

Soft-tissue and fluid changes associated with GH exposure may contribute to:

  • tingling;
  • numbness;
  • nerve-compression symptoms.

Long-Term Growth Signalling

Prolonged excessive growth hormone exposure may produce unwanted tissue-growth effects.

The source mentions concern regarding acromegaly-like changes and cardiovascular strain with prolonged excessive exposure.

Because growth hormone also increases IGF-1 signalling, long-term systemic exposure should not be described as risk-free.

What is Somatropin?

Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) composed of 191 amino acids.

It is designed to reproduce the biological activity of endogenous pituitary growth hormone.

Is Somatropin the same as HGH?

Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone and is commonly referred to as HGH or rhGH.

No.

Growth hormone stimulates IGF-1 production, but the two are different hormones with different receptors and physiological functions.

How does Somatropin work?

Somatropin activates the growth hormone receptor, triggering JAK2/STAT5 and related intracellular signalling.

It also increases downstream production of IGF-1.
