tabs.title: Description
tabs.html:
Pinealon is a synthetic short-chain peptide bioregulator composed of three amino acids:

Glu–Asp–Arg (EDR)

It has been investigated primarily in neuroprotection, cognitive biology, cellular stress responses, neuronal gene regulation, and ageing-related research.

The supplied material describes Pinealon as originating from the Russian peptide-bioregulator research tradition and discusses experimental findings involving:

  • neuronal oxidative stress;
  • hypoxic injury;
  • apoptosis;
  • mitochondrial function;
  • gene-expression regulation;
  • cognitive performance;
  • circadian biology;
  • age-related cellular changes.

The Atlas Longevity Pinealon pen contains 20 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

The evidence base for Pinealon is substantially more limited than that of established neurological medicines. Most of the supplied research is animal, in-vitro, or observational, with no established large-scale randomized human evidence or regulatory approval.

Clinical / Research Status

Pinealon remains an investigational peptide bioregulator.

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized clinical research Not established
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval No

The supplied material discusses limited human observational findings alongside a larger body of preclinical research.

Claims involving cognitive enhancement, neuroprotection, longevity, sleep improvement, or anti-ageing should therefore remain experimental rather than established therapeutic claims.

Evidence Type

The source describes research involving:

  • aged-animal cognitive models;
  • cultured cortical neurons;
  • accelerated-ageing mouse models;
  • human fibroblast cultures;
  • neurotoxicity models;
  • limited elderly observational research;
  • ischemia-reperfusion models;
  • sleep-deprivation behavioural models.

These studies investigate different biological endpoints and should not all be interpreted as equivalent evidence of human clinical efficacy.

Mechanism of Action

Pinealon is investigated as a cell-penetrating tripeptide bioregulator.

The supplied material proposes that the Glu-Asp-Arg sequence may interact with cellular and nuclear regulatory systems involved in neuronal survival and stress responses.

Reported research mechanisms include:

  • modulation of gene expression;
  • regulation of neuronal survival pathways;
  • oxidative-stress reduction;
  • mitochondrial stabilisation;
  • apoptosis-related signalling;
  • possible epigenetic effects;
  • changes in neurotransmitter-related pathways.

Gene-Expression Regulation

One of Pinealon’s defining research concepts is its proposed ability to influence transcription of genes involved in:

  • neuronal survival;
  • antioxidant defence;
  • apoptosis;
  • cellular adaptation.

The exact molecular interactions and their relevance in humans remain incompletely established.

Oxidative-Stress Research

Experimental work described in the source reports changes in:

  • reactive oxygen species;
  • antioxidant enzyme activity;
  • mitochondrial integrity;
  • stress-related cellular survival.

Neurotransmitter Research

The supplied material also discusses possible effects on serotonin metabolism and related neuronal signalling.

These mechanisms remain exploratory.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Cognitive Function Research

Pinealon has been studied in aged and stressed experimental models involving:

  • memory;
  • learning;
  • attention;
  • reaction time;
  • cognitive performance.

The source reports improvements in selected cognitive endpoints in animal models and limited observational research.

These findings do not establish Pinealon as a clinically proven cognitive enhancer.

Neuroprotection Research

A major Pinealon research area involves neuronal responses to:

  • oxidative stress;
  • hypoxia;
  • excitotoxicity;
  • neurotoxic exposure;
  • ischemic injury.

Experimental findings described by the source include reduced markers of neuronal damage and improved survival in selected models.

Oxidative-Stress Biology

The source discusses Pinealon in relation to endogenous antioxidant systems including:

  • superoxide dismutase;
  • catalase;
  • mitochondrial defence mechanisms.

These findings are mainly preclinical.

Apoptosis Research

Experimental models have examined whether Pinealon can influence programmed cell-death signalling under cellular stress.

Research described by the source includes changes in apoptosis-related pathways and neuronal survival markers.

Mitochondrial Research

Pinealon has also been investigated for possible effects on:

  • mitochondrial integrity;
  • oxidative damage;
  • energy-related cellular resilience.

This is particularly relevant to neurodegeneration and ageing models.

Cellular Ageing Research

The supplied material discusses Pinealon as a peptide bioregulator involved in experimental ageing research.

Reported areas include:

  • cellular longevity;
  • telomerase-related activity;
  • telomere biology;
  • age-related gene-expression changes.

These findings do not establish extension of human lifespan or reversal of human ageing.

Circadian Rhythm Research

Pinealon has also been investigated in relation to:

  • pineal biology;
  • melatonin-associated rhythms;
  • sleep-wake regulation;
  • circadian signalling.

The evidence described remains limited and primarily experimental.

Stress-Response Research

Animal models have investigated Pinealon during physical or psychological stress.

The source proposes effects involving:

  • HPA-axis signalling;
  • cellular adaptation;
  • cognitive resilience.

These are research observations rather than established therapeutic effects.

Retinal and Visual Research

The supplied material also discusses experimental retinal models involving:

  • photoreceptor preservation;
  • ischemic stress;
  • electrophysiological responses;
  • age-related retinal changes.

Human ophthalmological efficacy is not established.

Research Data

Aged rat cognitive models Increased memory retention and learning-related performance
Cultured cortical neurons Reduced oxidative-stress markers and increased neuronal survival under hypoxic stress
Accelerated-ageing mouse models Changes in lifespan and preservation of selected cognitive endpoints
Human fibroblast culture Increased telomerase-related activity and telomere-associated measurements
Rotenone neurotoxicity model Reduced apoptosis and improved mitochondrial integrity
Elderly observational research Changes in attention, recall and psycho-emotional measures
Rat ischemia-reperfusion model Reduced injury-related measurements and altered neuroprotective gene expression
Sleep-deprivation model Changes in circadian markers and cognitive-stress outcomes

Most of these findings are preclinical, and the limited observational evidence should not be treated as proof of clinical effectiveness.

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied material discusses experimental research combinations involving:

  • Pinealon + Epitalon;
  • Pinealon + Cerebrolysin;
  • Pinealon + Semax;
  • Pinealon + SS-31.

The proposed rationale involves combining pathways related to:

  • neuroprotection;
  • mitochondrial biology;
  • neurotrophic signalling;
  • circadian regulation;
  • cellular ageing.

The supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated strictly as experimental research concepts.

It is not an instruction to divide, repeat, or administer multiple injections.

The source’s daily schedules, frequency, duration, cycle intervals, and “biohacker” protocols should not be reproduced as human self-administration instructions.

The supplied material describes relatively few adverse effects, but the human evidence base is limited and does not establish a complete safety profile.

Reported observations include:

  • transient mild headache;
  • localized injection-site redness or irritation;
  • occasional drowsiness;
  • altered sleep patterns;
  • mild gastrointestinal discomfort.

Human Safety Evidence

The source states that significant hormonal, hepatic, or neurotoxic adverse effects have not been identified in available preclinical research.

However, absence of an adverse signal in limited preclinical or observational data does not establish safety in humans.

Important uncertainties include:

  • long-term systemic exposure;
  • neurological interactions;
  • psychiatric medication interactions;
  • other CNS-active compounds;
  • reproductive exposure;
  • effects in neurological disease;
  • repeated combination protocols.

Rapid Metabolism Claim

The supplied material suggests that Pinealon may be metabolized into its constituent amino acids because it is a short tripeptide.

That structural characteristic may influence degradation, but it should not be used to imply guaranteed safety.

tabs.html:
Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin Blend 30mg Bali

Dual Growth Hormone Signalling Research Blend

The Tesamorelin 20mg + Ipamorelin 10mg Blend combines two peptides with distinct mechanisms associated with growth hormone release.

Tesamorelin acts through the GHRH receptor, while ipamorelin acts through the growth hormone secretagogue receptor, also known as GHS-R1a.

The individual compounds have been investigated in endocrine research, but the safety and effectiveness of this specific 30mg combination have not been established in adequate human clinical trials.

What’s Inside the 30mg Blend?

Ingredient Quantity Research Focus
Tesamorelin 20mg GHRH receptor and growth hormone signalling

Total 30mg Experimental dual-peptide formulation

What Is Tesamorelin?

Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone.

It stimulates growth hormone release through GHRH receptor activity.

A specific pharmaceutical formulation of tesamorelin is approved in the United States for reducing excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy.

That approval does not extend automatically to independently manufactured tesamorelin vials, other indications or tesamorelin-ipamorelin blends.

Tesamorelin research has included:

  • Growth hormone secretion
  • IGF-1 signalling
  • Visceral adipose tissue measurements
  • Endocrine regulation
  • Metabolic outcomes

What Is Ipamorelin?

Ipamorelin is an experimental peptide that acts as an agonist at the growth hormone secretagogue receptor.

It has been investigated for its ability to influence growth hormone release.

Research areas include:

  • Growth hormone secretagogue activity
  • Ghrelin receptor signalling
  • Endocrine responses
  • Pituitary hormone regulation
  • Growth hormone pulse dynamics

Ipamorelin is not an established approved treatment for muscle growth, fat loss or recovery.

Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin Research Areas

The individual compounds have been investigated in relation to:

  • Growth hormone signalling
  • GHRH receptor activity
  • Ghrelin receptor activity
  • IGF-1 regulation
  • Endocrine responses
  • Metabolic pathways
  • Body composition research

These areas do not demonstrate that combining tesamorelin and ipamorelin produces greater benefits than either compound individually.

Tesamorelin vs Ipamorelin

Feature Tesamorelin Ipamorelin
Compound Class GHRH analogue Growth hormone secretagogue
Primary Receptor GHRH receptor GHS-R1a
Main Research Area GH and IGF-1 signalling GH secretagogue signalling
Quantity in Blend 20mg 10mg

Although the compounds act through different receptors, additive or synergistic effects of this specific blend have not been clinically established.

Safety Information

Tesamorelin can increase IGF-1 levels and may affect glucose regulation. Approved tesamorelin formulations carry warnings and require medical monitoring.

The safety profile of ipamorelin remains inadequately established.

Potential interactions, adverse effects and long-term risks of this combined formulation are not sufficiently characterised.

What is Ipamorelin researched for?

Ipamorelin has been investigated for its effects on growth hormone secretion through the ghrelin receptor.

What is the difference between Tesamorelin and Ipamorelin?

Tesamorelin activates GHRH receptors, while ipamorelin activates growth hormone secretagogue receptors. They influence growth hormone signalling through different mechanisms.

Is Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin the same as CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin?

No. Tesamorelin and CJC-1295 are different GHRH-related peptides. These blends have different compositions and cannot be assumed to have equivalent effects.

Does Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin increase growth hormone?

Both ingredients have been investigated for growth hormone-related activity, but the response and safety of this specific combined formulation have not been adequately established.

No. Although a specific pharmaceutical formulation of tesamorelin has an approved indication for HIV-associated abdominal fat, that evidence does not establish effectiveness for this blend or general abdominal fat reduction.

Is Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin approved for medical use?

Is this blend suitable for injection?

5-Amino-1MQ 100 mg Pen

Product Description

5-Amino-1MQ is a synthetic small-molecule compound studied primarily as an inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme involved in nicotinamide metabolism, cellular methylation pathways, and NAD+ biology.

Interest in 5-Amino-1MQ research is largely driven by the relationship between NNMT activity and metabolic regulation. Preclinical models have investigated whether reducing NNMT activity can influence cellular NAD+ availability, mitochondrial energy metabolism, adipose-tissue biology, glucose regulation, and lipid handling.

The Atlas Longevity 5-Amino-1MQ pen contains 100 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge, providing 300 measurable pen units for precise research calculations.

5-Amino-1MQ remains an investigational compound. The supplied reference material does not establish it as an approved treatment for obesity, weight management, metabolic disease, anti-ageing, or any other medical condition.

Clinical / Research Status

5-Amino-1MQ is best described as an experimental research compound.

The supplied material discusses its investigation in metabolic research, particularly around obesity-related biology, insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial function, NAD+ metabolism, and adipose-tissue regulation. However, the evidence classification supplied with the product specifically identifies animal and in-vitro research, rather than completed human randomized controlled trials or established regulatory evidence.

Accordingly, findings from animal or cellular models should not be interpreted as established clinical outcomes in humans.

Current evidence status based on the supplied material:

Evidence Category Status

Human observational evidence Not established in supplied evidence
Animal research Yes
In-vitro / cellular research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Evidence Type

The most clearly supported evidence supplied for 5-Amino-1MQ comes from:

  • Animal metabolic models, including diet-induced obesity and high-fat-diet research.
  • In-vitro research, including adipocyte and cellular metabolic models.
  • Mechanistic research involving NNMT, NAD+, SAM, mitochondrial activity, lipid metabolism, and glucose regulation.

Although the reference describes emerging interest in human applications, it does not provide enough clinical-trial detail to classify the compound as having established human efficacy.

Mechanism of Action

5-Amino-1MQ is researched for its ability to inhibit NNMT.

NNMT normally methylates nicotinamide, affecting how nicotinamide is processed within cells. Because nicotinamide participates in NAD+ metabolism, inhibiting NNMT may alter the amount of nicotinamide available for NAD+ salvage pathways.

In experimental systems, this has been associated with changes in:

  • intracellular NAD+ availability;
  • mitochondrial respiration;
  • ATP-related energy metabolism;
  • lipid oxidation and storage;
  • adipocyte metabolism;
  • glucose regulation;
  • methylation pathways involving S-adenosylmethionine, or SAM.

The scientific interest is therefore not simply in “fat burning.” Researchers are studying NNMT as part of a broader metabolic network connecting energy production, nutrient handling, mitochondrial function, and cellular methylation.

These mechanisms remain an area of active experimental research.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Adipose-Tissue Metabolism

NNMT is expressed in metabolically active tissues, including white adipose tissue.

In diet-induced obesity models, NNMT inhibition has been associated with reductions in adipose accumulation and changes in pathways involved in lipid storage and energy expenditure. These findings make 5-Amino-1MQ relevant to research investigating how adipocytes regulate energy balance.

These findings are preclinical and should not be interpreted as proof of weight-loss efficacy in humans.

NAD+ Metabolism

One of the central areas of 5-Amino-1MQ research involves the relationship between NNMT inhibition and cellular NAD+ metabolism.

Experimental work described in the supplied material suggests that suppressing NNMT activity may reduce nicotinamide methylation and increase nicotinamide availability for NAD+-related pathways.

Because NAD+ participates in cellular redox reactions and energy metabolism, this mechanism has generated interest in mitochondrial and metabolic research.

Mitochondrial Function and Cellular Energy

Preclinical research has also examined changes in mitochondrial respiration and ATP-related energy production following NNMT inhibition.

The research interest centres on whether altered NAD+ availability and cellular redox balance can influence mitochondrial efficiency under metabolic stress.

Claims of increased human energy, endurance, or anti-ageing effects cannot be established from these preclinical findings alone.

Glucose Metabolism

Animal studies described in the supplied source report changes in fasting glucose, insulin levels, glucose tolerance, and insulin sensitivity following experimental NNMT inhibition.

This makes 5-Amino-1MQ relevant to metabolic research involving glucose regulation, but these findings do not establish it as a treatment for diabetes or insulin resistance.

Lipid Metabolism

5-Amino-1MQ has also been investigated for possible effects on lipid storage and oxidation.

Animal and cellular models described in the source reported reduced lipid accumulation, changes in hepatic triglycerides, and increased markers associated with fatty-acid utilization.

Additional human research would be needed before these findings could be translated into clinical claims.

Lean-Tissue and Body-Composition Research

The supplied reference describes animal studies in which reductions in adipose tissue occurred without a proportional loss of lean mass.

This is an interesting metabolic research finding, but it does not establish that 5-Amino-1MQ preserves muscle mass in humans.

Metabolic Inflammation

Obesity-related experimental models have also explored how NNMT inhibition may influence inflammatory signalling within adipose tissue.

The supplied reference reports changes involving inflammatory markers including TNF-α and IL-6.

These observations remain preclinical.

SAM, Methylation and Longevity Research

NNMT activity is connected not only with nicotinamide metabolism but also with S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) utilization.

For this reason, inhibition of NNMT is being studied in relation to cellular methylation balance and metabolic gene regulation. The supplied material links this pathway with broader longevity and cellular-ageing research.

This should be regarded as a mechanistic research area rather than evidence that 5-Amino-1MQ extends human lifespan.

Research Data

The following findings are reported in the supplied research material and primarily represent animal or cellular evidence.

The supplied reference reports a particularly large body-weight change in one diet-induced obesity mouse model. Because this is an animal result, it should not be extrapolated into an expected percentage of human weight loss.

Potential Combination Research

5-Amino-1MQ and NAD+ Pathway Research

The supplied material discusses experimental interest in combining NNMT inhibition with approaches intended to increase NAD+ availability.

The proposed research rationale is that the two approaches act at different points within related metabolic pathways: one may influence NAD+ precursor utilization through NNMT inhibition, while the other aims to increase the available NAD+ pool.

The reference also reports experimental combination research involving NAD+ and 5-Amino-1MQ.

However, the supplied information does not establish the clinical safety, efficacy, compatibility, or optimal dosing of such combinations in humans.

Other compound combinations suggested by the original source have not been carried into this Atlas Longevity page because sufficient supporting combination evidence was not supplied.

A reliable human adverse-effect profile cannot be established from the supplied evidence.

The original material describes 5-Amino-1MQ as generally tolerated in preclinical models and lists possible effects including fatigue, nausea, digestive discomfort, headache, and local injection-site irritation. However, it does not provide sufficient human clinical-study information, incidence rates, study populations, or controlled safety data to establish these as documented human adverse reactions.

These statements therefore should not be interpreted as a complete safety profile.

Long-term human safety, contraindications, medication interactions, reproductive effects, and the safety of combination protocols are not established by the supplied research material.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is 5-Amino-1MQ?

5-Amino-1MQ is a synthetic small molecule being researched primarily as an inhibitor of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase, or NNMT.

Researchers are investigating this pathway because NNMT interacts with nicotinamide, NAD+ metabolism, cellular methylation, adipose biology, and mitochondrial energy metabolism.

Is 5-Amino-1MQ a peptide?

No. Despite sometimes being discussed alongside research peptides, the supplied chemical information classifies 5-Amino-1MQ as a synthetic small molecule, not an amino-acid peptide sequence.

How does 5-Amino-1MQ work?

5-Amino-1MQ inhibits NNMT.

In experimental systems, reducing NNMT activity can alter nicotinamide metabolism and may increase the availability of nicotinamide for NAD+-related cellular pathways.

Researchers are studying the downstream effects of this mechanism on mitochondrial function, lipid metabolism, glucose regulation, and cellular energy production.

What is 5-Amino-1MQ being researched for?

Not from the evidence supplied for this page.

The source provides experimental protocol suggestions, but it does not provide sufficient controlled human clinical evidence to establish them as validated medical dosing standards.

Has 5-Amino-1MQ been proven to cause weight loss in humans?

The supplied material does not establish that conclusion.

Animal models have reported reductions in body weight and adipose tissue following NNMT inhibition, but animal results cannot be assumed to produce equivalent outcomes in humans.

Can 5-Amino-1MQ be researched alongside NAD+?

Ipamorelin 10 mg Pen

Product Description

Ipamorelin is a selective growth hormone secretagogue peptide from the GHRP family, studied primarily for its interaction with the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a).

By activating ghrelin-sensitive receptors within the pituitary and related neuroendocrine pathways, Ipamorelin has been investigated for its ability to stimulate pulsatile endogenous growth hormone (GH) release rather than supplying growth hormone directly.

Compared with earlier growth hormone-releasing peptides, Ipamorelin is particularly interesting because of its relatively selective receptor profile and the lower cortisol and prolactin responses reported in experimental research. Pasted text

Research areas include growth hormone signalling, IGF-1 biology, recovery pathways, endocrine ageing, sleep-associated hormone secretion, metabolism, and tissue repair.

The Atlas Longevity Ipamorelin pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Ipamorelin remains an investigational research peptide and should not be presented as an approved treatment for growth hormone deficiency, muscle growth, anti-ageing, sleep disorders, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

Ipamorelin has been investigated in animal models, laboratory studies, and exploratory human research.

The supplied material characterizes the evidence base as primarily preclinical with limited exploratory human data. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research Limited / exploratory
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Some human studies demonstrate pharmacological activity, but this should not be confused with regulatory approval or proven effectiveness for performance, recovery, anti-ageing, or body-composition purposes.

Evidence Type

The supplied research includes:

  • pituitary-cell studies;
  • healthy adult pharmacology studies;
  • aged-animal models;
  • postoperative gastrointestinal research;
  • bone-related animal models;
  • catabolic-state animal studies;
  • in-vitro somatotroph assays;
  • exploratory human growth hormone research. Pasted text

Evidence quality and clinical relevance differ considerably across these research areas.

Mechanism of Action

Ipamorelin primarily acts as an agonist of the GHS-R1a receptor, commonly known as the growth hormone secretagogue or ghrelin receptor.

Activation of this receptor can stimulate pituitary somatotroph cells to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile pattern.

This is different from administering growth hormone directly.

The supplied material describes Ipamorelin as being comparatively selective for GH stimulation, with less activation of cortisol- and prolactin-related pathways than some earlier GHRPs. Pasted text

Increased growth hormone signalling can subsequently influence hepatic production of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1), creating downstream effects on cellular growth, protein metabolism, connective-tissue biology, and metabolic signalling.

The extent and clinical significance of these effects depend on the model studied.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Endogenous Growth Hormone Research

Ipamorelin is primarily investigated for its ability to stimulate the body’s own growth hormone secretion.

Rather than replacing GH directly, the compound interacts with growth hormone secretagogue receptors to influence endogenous pituitary release.

This makes Ipamorelin useful in research examining GH pulse amplitude, timing, endocrine feedback, and downstream IGF-1 signalling. Pasted text

This mechanism does not establish Ipamorelin as an approved growth hormone treatment.

Recovery and Tissue-Repair Signalling

Growth hormone and IGF-1 participate in several processes involved in tissue adaptation and repair.

Ipamorelin research therefore includes experimental investigation of:

  • protein metabolism;
  • connective-tissue biology;
  • muscle-repair pathways;
  • structural tissue adaptation;
  • regenerative signalling. Pasted text

These mechanisms should not be interpreted as guaranteed improvements in human recovery or muscle gain.

Endocrine Feedback Research

A major research distinction between secretagogues and externally administered growth hormone is the way they interact with existing endocrine signalling.

The supplied source discusses Ipamorelin in relation to maintaining endogenous hypothalamic-pituitary regulation while stimulating pituitary GH release. Pasted text

The long-term clinical implications of this distinction are not established by the supplied information.

Selective Growth Hormone Secretagogue Research

Earlier growth hormone-releasing peptides can affect several endocrine pathways.

Ipamorelin was developed and studied for a more selective secretagogue profile.

Experimental research suggests that it can stimulate GH with relatively limited effects on ACTH, cortisol, and prolactin compared with some less-selective GHRPs. Pasted text

“More selective” should not be interpreted as having no endocrine effects or no potential risks.

Sleep-Associated Hormone Research

Growth hormone secretion follows a natural pulsatile rhythm, with significant secretion associated with deep sleep.

Ipamorelin has therefore been investigated in research examining nocturnal GH pulses, endocrine timing, sleep-associated hormone biology, and recovery signalling. Pasted text

The supplied evidence does not establish Ipamorelin as a treatment for insomnia or poor sleep quality.

IGF-1 Signalling

Growth hormone can stimulate hepatic production of IGF-1.

This places Ipamorelin within research involving the broader GH–IGF-1 axis and downstream biological pathways related to:

  • cellular growth;
  • protein metabolism;
  • tissue repair;
  • skeletal biology;
  • metabolic signalling. Pasted text

Effects on these pathways do not guarantee anabolic or performance outcomes in humans.

Age-Associated GH Research

Endogenous growth hormone secretion can change with age.

Ipamorelin has therefore been investigated in experimental models examining age-associated changes in GH pulsatility and endocrine signalling. Pasted text

This should not be interpreted as evidence that Ipamorelin reverses ageing or restores youthful physiology in humans.

Gastrointestinal Motility Research

The supplied research also references human clinical investigation involving postoperative ileus and gastrointestinal motility. Pasted text

This represents a distinct clinical research area and should not be used as evidence for muscle growth, longevity, recovery, or other unrelated claims.

Is Ipamorelin growth hormone?

How does Ipamorelin work?

Ipamorelin activates the GHS-R1a / ghrelin receptor.

AOD-9604 5 mg Pen

Product Description

AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide fragment derived from the C-terminal region of human growth hormone and developed for research into the metabolic signalling associated with fat metabolism.

Unlike full-length growth hormone, AOD-9604 was designed to investigate specific metabolic actions without reproducing the broader growth-promoting activity associated with HGH. Research has focused particularly on lipolysis, lipogenesis, adipose-tissue metabolism, metabolic regulation, and body-composition pathways. Pasted text

AOD-9604 has also attracted research interest outside metabolic biology, including experimental investigation of cartilage, connective tissue, fibroblast activity, and tissue-repair mechanisms. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity AOD-9604 pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total selectable units/clicks.

Clinical / Research Status

AOD-9604 has been investigated in both human and preclinical research, including studies related to obesity, metabolic regulation and safety.

Based on the supplied reference material, the evidence base includes:

Evidence Type Status
Human randomized clinical trials Yes
Observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

The presence of human research does not mean AOD-9604 is an approved treatment for obesity, fat loss, joint conditions, or other medical conditions.

Experimental and preclinical findings should also not be interpreted as guaranteed human outcomes.

Evidence Type

Research discussed in the supplied material includes:

  • controlled human safety and metabolic studies;
  • obesity-related human clinical research;
  • animal models of obesity and high-fat-diet exposure;
  • adipocyte and cellular research;
  • comparative research involving growth hormone;
  • experimental connective-tissue and cartilage investigation. Pasted text

Evidence strength varies considerably between these areas. Metabolic mechanisms observed in cells or animals should not automatically be treated as established clinical benefits.

Mechanism of Action

AOD-9604 represents a modified growth-hormone fragment associated with the hormone’s metabolic region.

Its principal research mechanism involves the regulation of two opposing processes:

Lipolysis — the breakdown of stored triglycerides into fatty acids that can become available for cellular energy metabolism.

Lipogenesis — the creation and storage of new fat within adipose tissue.

The supplied research also associates AOD-9604 with beta-adrenergic signalling and AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), both of which are relevant to cellular energy regulation and lipid metabolism. Pasted text

A key area of scientific interest is whether these metabolic effects can be studied independently from the broader anabolic and endocrine actions of full-length growth hormone.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Fat Metabolism Research

AOD-9604 is primarily investigated for its effects on adipose-tissue metabolism.

Experimental research has examined whether the peptide can increase the mobilisation of stored lipids while simultaneously reducing pathways involved in new lipid accumulation.

This makes AOD-9604 relevant to research investigating lipolysis, fatty-acid utilisation and metabolic regulation. Pasted text

These mechanisms should not be interpreted as a guarantee of fat loss in humans.

Adipose-Tissue Regulation

Animal and early human research described in the supplied material has investigated changes in abdominal and visceral adipose tissue.

The proposed mechanism involves altered lipolytic signalling and increased utilisation of fatty acids within metabolically active tissues. Pasted text

Claims of reliable or “site-specific” human fat reduction would require stronger clinical evidence than the source provides.

Body-Composition Research

Some experimental studies have investigated whether reductions in adipose tissue can occur without corresponding reductions in lean tissue.

This has created research interest around AOD-9604 in body-composition models. Pasted text

However, preservation of muscle mass should not be presented as a guaranteed effect in humans.

Lipid and Glucose Metabolism

AOD-9604 research has also examined markers associated with:

  • lipid utilisation;
  • glucose handling;
  • insulin-related metabolic pathways;
  • circulating lipid levels;
  • cellular energy balance. Pasted text

The supplied evidence does not establish AOD-9604 as a treatment for diabetes, insulin resistance, cholesterol disorders or other metabolic diseases.

Growth Hormone Fragment Research

One reason AOD-9604 remains scientifically interesting is its relationship with growth hormone biology.

It was developed to investigate whether metabolic signalling associated with the C-terminal region of HGH could be studied without reproducing the full spectrum of growth-hormone activity.

This includes particular interest in whether metabolic effects can occur without substantial changes in IGF-1 or carbohydrate regulation. Pasted text

Mitochondrial and Energy Metabolism

Greater availability of fatty acids for oxidation can influence mitochondrial energy metabolism.

For this reason, AOD-9604 has also been investigated in research examining metabolic fuel utilisation, AMPK signalling and mitochondrial activity.

These findings remain mechanistic research rather than evidence that AOD-9604 reliably increases energy or endurance in humans.

Cartilage and Connective-Tissue Research

Research interest in AOD-9604 extends beyond adipose biology.

Cellular and animal studies referenced in the supplied material have investigated potential effects on cartilage repair, collagen-related pathways, fibroblast activity and connective-tissue regeneration. Pasted text

These findings are preliminary and should not be interpreted as established treatment effects for joint injuries or degenerative conditions.

Obesity mouse models Reduced adiposity and increased markers associated with lipolysis and fat oxidation
Human clinical research Weight-management and metabolic outcomes were investigated without reported changes in IGF-1 or glucose markers in the supplied summary
In-vitro adipocyte research Reduced lipogenesis and increased triglyceride breakdown were reported
High-fat-diet rat research Changes in thermogenesis, mitochondrial activity and AMPK signalling were reported

The supplied source includes both human and preclinical research, but the findings should be interpreted according to each study type rather than combined into a single claim of proven clinical efficacy. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The original source discusses experimental combinations involving AOD-9604 with compounds such as MOTS-c, L-carnitine, tesamorelin and incretin-related metabolic agents. Pasted text

However, the supplied material does not provide enough combination-specific clinical evidence to establish these combinations as safe or effective human protocols.

FAQs

What is AOD-9604?

AOD-9604 is a synthetic peptide derived from a region of human growth hormone associated with metabolic activity.

It is primarily researched for its potential influence on lipolysis, lipogenesis and adipose-tissue metabolism.

Is AOD-9604 the same as human growth hormone?

No.

AOD-9604 is a fragment associated with human growth hormone, rather than full-length HGH.

It has been researched specifically to investigate certain metabolic effects without recreating the complete hormonal activity of HGH.

How does AOD-9604 work?

AOD-9604 is researched primarily for its influence on lipolysis and lipogenesis.

Experimental evidence also links its activity with beta-adrenergic and AMPK-related metabolic pathways. Pasted text

What is AOD-9604 being researched for?

Research areas include:

  • adipose-tissue metabolism;
  • lipolysis;
  • lipid utilisation;
  • metabolic regulation;
  • body composition;
  • AMPK signalling;
  • mitochondrial metabolism;
  • cartilage and connective-tissue biology.

Evidence strength varies depending on the research area.

How much AOD-9604 is in each Atlas Longevity pen?

5 mg in 3 mL.

What is the concentration of the AOD-9604 pen?

How many clicks are in the pen?

300 total clicks.

How much AOD-9604 is in one click?

0.0167 mg

or:

How many clicks equal 0.25 mg?

15 clicks = 0.25 mg.

How many clicks equal 0.30 mg?

How many clicks equal 0.50 mg?

30 clicks = 0.50 mg.

How many clicks equal 1 mg?

60 clicks = 1 mg.

These values are concentration conversions rather than dosing recommendations.

How long does an AOD-9604 pen last?

The pen contains 300 total clicks, so duration depends on the number of clicks used per administration.

These examples describe pen capacity rather than recommended use.

Does the medication disappear when the dial returns to zero?

No.

After administration, the dial returns to zero while the unused product remains in the cartridge.

The cartridge continues to contain the remaining medication until its total 300 units have been used.

Has AOD-9604 been studied in humans?

Yes. The supplied reference identifies human randomized clinical research and human tolerability research alongside animal and in-vitro studies. Pasted text

However, clinical research should not be confused with regulatory approval or proof of effectiveness for a particular medical condition.

The supplied material does not provide evidence of regulatory approval for AOD-9604 as a weight-loss treatment.

tabs.title: Description
tabs.html:
DSIP 5 mg Pen

Product Description

DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide) is an endogenous nonapeptide originally identified during research into delta-wave sleep and neurophysiological sleep regulation.

The peptide has since been investigated across several research areas involving sleep architecture, circadian signalling, hypothalamic function, neuroendocrine regulation, and physiological stress responses.

Rather than functioning like a conventional sedative, DSIP is studied as a potential regulatory signal within neural and endocrine systems involved in sleep-stage coordination and stress-related hormone activity. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity DSIP pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

DSIP remains an investigational research peptide. The available evidence does not establish it as an approved treatment for insomnia, anxiety, stress disorders, endocrine conditions, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

DSIP has been investigated in animal, laboratory, observational, and limited controlled human research.

The supplied material characterizes the evidence base as primarily preclinical and exploratory, with only limited controlled human studies. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research Limited
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established in supplied material

The existence of early human research should not be interpreted as proof of therapeutic effectiveness.

Evidence Type

Research described in the supplied material includes:

  • rodent EEG and sleep studies;
  • animal stress-response models;
  • human insomnia observations and controlled studies;
  • opioid-withdrawal observations;
  • neuroendocrine research;
  • oxidative-stress laboratory models;
  • pituitary-hormone investigations;
  • animal pain-perception models. Pasted text

The level of evidence differs substantially between these research areas.

Mechanism of Action

The exact physiological role of DSIP remains incompletely defined.

Research has focused on whether DSIP interacts with central nervous system and neuroendocrine pathways involved in:

  • delta-wave sleep;
  • hypothalamic signalling;
  • pituitary activity;
  • stress-hormone regulation;
  • circadian coordination;
  • inhibitory neurotransmission;
  • endocrine rhythm synchronization. Pasted text

Unlike conventional hypnotic agents that directly suppress neural activity through well-defined receptor systems, DSIP is investigated more as a neuroregulatory peptide that may influence networks governing sleep and hormonal timing.

Its mechanisms remain under investigation and should not be presented as clinically established.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Delta-Wave and Slow-Wave Sleep Research

DSIP was originally identified during studies of delta-wave activity.

Slow-wave sleep is characterized by synchronized low-frequency brain activity and is an important component of normal sleep architecture.

Experimental DSIP research has examined whether the peptide can influence the duration, organization, or continuity of delta-dominant sleep phases. Pasted text

This does not establish DSIP as a proven treatment for insomnia.

Hypothalamic Signalling

The hypothalamus plays a central role in regulating:

  • sleep and wakefulness;
  • circadian rhythms;
  • pituitary signalling;
  • autonomic function;
  • endocrine responses.

DSIP has been investigated for potential interactions with hypothalamic regulatory pathways involved in coordinating these systems. Pasted text

Stress and HPA-Axis Research

The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis coordinates physiological stress responses through signalling involving CRH, ACTH, and cortisol.

Animal and exploratory research has examined whether DSIP can modify this signalling network and influence stress-related hormonal activity. Pasted text

These findings should not be interpreted as evidence that DSIP treats anxiety, chronic stress, or cortisol disorders.

Neurotransmitter Regulation

Sleep depends on a balance between excitatory and inhibitory neural signalling.

DSIP has been investigated for possible effects on central neurotransmitter balance, including pathways associated with inhibitory signalling.

Unlike conventional sedatives, the supplied material describes DSIP as potentially influencing these systems indirectly rather than acting as a direct receptor agonist. Pasted text

Circadian and Endocrine Rhythm Research

Sleep architecture and endocrine secretion are closely interconnected.

Hormones including growth hormone, cortisol, and melatonin follow circadian or sleep-associated patterns.

DSIP research has therefore explored whether changes in sleep architecture may interact with the timing of endocrine secretion. Pasted text

This remains a mechanistic research area rather than an established anti-ageing or hormonal therapy.

Stress-Adaptation Research

Chronic physiological stress can disrupt both sleep and neuroendocrine signalling.

DSIP has been examined experimentally in models of altered stress responses to determine whether it influences central regulatory pathways involved in adaptation.

The supplied material positions this as a neuroendocrine research area rather than direct pharmacological suppression of stress hormones. Pasted text

Neural Recovery and Sleep Architecture

Deep sleep is associated with several physiological processes involving neural recovery, memory consolidation, and endocrine timing.

Because DSIP is studied in relation to delta-wave activity, researchers have investigated its potential relevance to the interaction between sleep architecture and neuroendocrine recovery processes. Pasted text

Human clinical significance remains uncertain.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Rodent EEG sleep studies Increased delta-wave activity and changes in slow-wave sleep continuity
Stress-related animal models Reduced corticosteroid output and changes in HPA-axis activity
Chronic-insomnia observational research Improvements in subjective sleep onset and nocturnal awakening measures were reported
Opioid-withdrawal clinical observations Changes in withdrawal severity and autonomic measures were reported
In-vitro oxidative-stress models Changes in lipid-peroxidation and antioxidant markers
Animal neuroendocrine studies Changes in GH, LH and somatostatin secretion patterns
Rodent pain models Changes in nociceptive thresholds

These findings include animal, laboratory, observational, and limited human evidence and should not be treated as equivalent levels of proof. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combination concepts involving DSIP with:

  • Epitalon;
  • Selank;
  • Semax;
  • GHK-Cu. Pasted text

These combinations are proposed around research themes such as circadian signalling, stress-response pathways, cognitive biology, and recovery.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

Atlas Longevity therefore does not present them as recommended protocols.

What Is Kisspeptin-10?

Kisspeptin-10 is a 10-amino-acid fragment of kisspeptin with biological activity at the KISS1 receptor (KISS1R).

Kisspeptin-10 should not, however, be confused with an approved hormone replacement or fertility treatment.

tabs.html:
Epithalon 20 mg Pen

Product Description

Epithalon, also known as Epitalon, is a synthetic tetrapeptide composed of four amino acids: alanine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid, and glycine (AEDG).

It originates from research involving epithalamin, a pineal-derived preparation investigated in ageing biology. Epithalon subsequently became a subject of experimental research focused on telomerase activity, telomere biology, cellular senescence, circadian signalling, oxidative stress, and longevity-related cellular pathways. Pasted text

One of its best-known research areas involves whether Epithalon can influence telomerase, an enzyme involved in maintaining telomeric DNA at chromosome ends during cellular replication.

The Atlas Longevity Epithalon pen contains 20 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Epithalon remains an investigational research peptide and should not be presented as an approved anti-ageing, longevity, sleep, or medical treatment.

Clinical / Research Status

Epithalon has primarily been investigated in preclinical, laboratory, and regional ageing research, with limited exploratory human evidence.

The supplied material describes the available evidence as follows: Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research Limited
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Human observations should not be treated as equivalent to large, independently replicated randomized clinical trials.

Similarly, laboratory evidence involving telomerase or cellular lifespan cannot be translated directly into claims of increased human lifespan.

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • human somatic-cell studies;
  • telomerase and telomere-length experiments;
  • animal longevity models;
  • pineal and circadian research;
  • observational human ageing studies;
  • oxidative-stress experiments;
  • retinal injury models;
  • immunosenescence research. Pasted text

Evidence strength varies significantly between these areas.

Mechanism of Action

Epithalon is primarily researched for its potential influence on telomerase activity and telomere biology.

Telomeres are repetitive DNA structures located at chromosome ends. They protect chromosomes during cellular replication but generally become progressively shorter as cells divide.

Telomerase is an enzyme capable of extending telomeric DNA.

Laboratory studies referenced in the supplied material have investigated whether Epithalon can increase telomerase activity and influence telomere maintenance in dividing human cells. Pasted text

Beyond telomere biology, Epithalon has also been explored in research involving:

  • cellular senescence;
  • chromosomal stability;
  • pineal signalling;
  • melatonin rhythms;
  • oxidative-stress responses;
  • circadian regulation.

The precise biological effects and their relevance to human ageing remain under investigation.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Telomerase Activation Research

Epithalon is particularly associated with experimental research into telomerase activation.

In laboratory cell models, researchers have investigated whether Epithalon can influence telomerase activity and consequently affect telomere length in dividing cells. Pasted text

These results are scientifically interesting, but increased telomerase activity in cultured cells does not demonstrate that Epithalon extends human lifespan.

Telomere Maintenance

Telomeres progressively shorten during repeated cell division.

Because critically shortened telomeres can contribute to replicative senescence, researchers have investigated whether maintaining telomeric DNA could influence cellular ageing processes.

Epithalon’s proposed influence on this pathway places it within telomere-maintenance and cellular-ageing research.

Genomic Stability Research

Telomere dysfunction can contribute to chromosomal instability and altered cellular behaviour.

Epithalon is therefore studied in experimental models examining relationships between telomere integrity, chromosome protection, and genomic stability. Pasted text

This remains a mechanistic research area rather than an established clinical benefit.

Cellular Senescence

Cellular senescence occurs when cells enter a persistent state of growth arrest and undergo changes in gene expression and signalling.

Because telomere shortening can contribute to senescence, researchers have explored whether telomerase-related mechanisms influenced by Epithalon may affect the timing or characteristics of cellular ageing. Pasted text

Pineal and Circadian Research

Epithalon originated from research involving epithalamin and pineal-gland biology.

The pineal gland participates in circadian regulation and melatonin secretion, creating a second major area of Epithalon research beyond telomere biology.

Experimental work has investigated potential effects on:

  • melatonin rhythms;
  • sleep-related endocrine timing;
  • pineal activity;
  • circadian synchronization. Pasted text

Evidence does not establish Epithalon as an approved treatment for insomnia or circadian-rhythm disorders.

Oxidative-Stress Research

Oxidative stress can contribute to cellular injury and may accelerate telomere attrition.

Laboratory research involving Epithalon has therefore examined markers of oxidative stress alongside telomere and ageing-related pathways. Pasted text

The supplied material reports changes in lipid-peroxidation markers and antioxidant-related activity in experimental models.

Replicative Lifespan Research

Cellular experiments have investigated whether alterations in telomerase activity can influence the number of times certain cells can divide before entering replicative senescence.

This has led to Epithalon being discussed in cellular lifespan and longevity research. Pasted text

Cellular lifespan should not be confused with organism or human lifespan.

Integrated Ageing Biology

Ageing involves multiple interacting biological processes rather than one isolated pathway.

The supplied research positions Epithalon at the intersection of:

  • telomere biology;
  • cellular senescence;
  • oxidative stress;
  • circadian regulation;
  • pineal signalling;
  • age-associated cellular changes. Pasted text

For this reason, it remains of interest in experimental longevity research despite significant unanswered clinical questions.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Human somatic-cell culture Increased telomerase activity and changes in telomere length
Aged mouse longevity models Changes in median lifespan and age-associated tumour incidence were reported
Pineal-gland animal models Changes in melatonin secretion rhythm and circadian markers
Elderly observational cohort Changes in sleep measures and nocturnal melatonin were reported
Rat retinal-degeneration model Reduced photoreceptor loss and changes in retinal integrity
In-vitro oxidative-stress studies Reduced lipid-peroxidation markers and altered antioxidant-enzyme expression
Rodent immunosenescence research Changes in T-cell function and thymic activity

These studies include in-vitro, animal, and observational human evidence and should not be treated as equivalent levels of clinical proof. Pasted text

In particular, longevity findings in rodents should not be converted into predictions of increased lifespan in humans.

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied reference discusses experimental combination concepts involving Epithalon with:

  • BPC-157;
  • GHK-Cu;
  • NAD+;
  • Thymalin. Pasted text

These combinations are discussed around research themes including telomere biology, tissue regeneration, extracellular-matrix biology, mitochondrial metabolism, pineal signalling, and immunosenescence.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be considered experimental research concepts rather than recommended protocols.

Possible Side Effects

Human safety evidence for Epithalon remains limited.

The supplied material describes reported effects including:

  • temporary drowsiness;
  • mild fatigue;
  • localized redness or tenderness;
  • headache;
  • temporary changes in sleep patterns. Pasted text

The source also reports an absence of certain hormonal, hepatic, or systemic adverse effects within available research.

However, limited detection of adverse effects should not be interpreted as proof of safety.

The supplied material does not establish a comprehensive understanding of:

  • long-term human safety;
  • contraindications;
  • medication interactions;
  • reproductive effects;
  • cancer-related risks;
  • consequences of prolonged telomerase modulation;
  • risks associated with combination research.

The last point is especially important because telomerase biology is complex; increasing telomerase activity should not automatically be characterized as universally beneficial.

Product Description

GHK-Cu (Glycyl-L-Histidyl-L-Lysine Copper Complex) is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide studied for its role in tissue repair, extracellular-matrix regulation, wound healing, skin biology, and cellular signalling.

The peptide binds copper ions and has been investigated for its influence on collagen and elastin production, fibroblast activity, angiogenesis, antioxidant defence, inflammatory signalling, and tissue remodelling. Pasted text

GHK-Cu is also of interest in research examining gene-expression patterns associated with repair, metabolism, immune signalling, fibrosis, skin ageing, and cellular regeneration.

The Atlas Longevity GHK-Cu pen contains 100 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

GHK-Cu should not be presented as an approved injectable treatment for skin ageing, wound healing, hair loss, fibrosis, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

GHK-Cu has been investigated across human, animal, and in-vitro research, including dermatological, cosmetic, wound-healing, fibroblast, and regenerative models.

The supplied reference classifies the evidence as follows: Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Human research involving topical or cosmetic GHK-Cu formulations should not automatically be treated as evidence for the clinical effectiveness or safety of a pre-mixed injection pen.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • human dermal fibroblasts;
  • human skin and gene-expression profiling;
  • animal wound-healing models;
  • hair-follicle cell cultures;
  • UV-damaged skin models;
  • antioxidant assays;
  • topical and subcutaneous research;
  • extracellular-matrix and tissue-remodelling studies. Pasted text

Evidence strength varies significantly depending on the formulation, route of exposure, study model, and outcome being measured.

Mechanism of Action

GHK-Cu is formed when the GHK tripeptide binds a copper ion.

Copper participates in numerous enzymes involved in tissue repair, antioxidant defence, extracellular-matrix turnover, and normal cellular function.

Experimental research described in the supplied material suggests GHK-Cu may influence:

  • collagen I and III expression;
  • elastin-related pathways;
  • fibroblast activity;
  • metalloproteinases involved in matrix turnover;
  • antioxidant enzymes such as superoxide dismutase;
  • inflammatory pathways including NF-κB;
  • angiogenesis;
  • wound contraction and epithelial repair. Pasted text

The source also describes broad gene-expression effects, although claims involving thousands of genes should be interpreted as transcriptomic research rather than proof of thousands of distinct clinical benefits.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Collagen and Extracellular-Matrix Research

GHK-Cu is widely investigated for its effects on fibroblasts and extracellular-matrix proteins.

Experimental models have reported increased production of collagen and elastin, making the peptide relevant to research examining skin structure, connective tissue, wound healing, and matrix remodelling. Pasted text

These findings should not be interpreted as guaranteed improvements in human skin quality following injectable use.

Wound-Healing Research

GHK-Cu has been investigated in wound models involving:

  • fibroblast proliferation;
  • keratinocyte migration;
  • epithelial repair;
  • angiogenesis;
  • extracellular-matrix formation.

Animal studies described in the supplied source report accelerated wound closure and changes in vascular and epithelial repair pathways. Pasted text

Human therapeutic wound-healing efficacy is not established by this evidence.

Anti-Inflammatory and Antioxidant Research

Experimental research has examined how GHK-Cu may influence oxidative stress and inflammatory signalling.

The supplied source reports changes involving:

  • IL-6;
  • TNF-α;
  • superoxide dismutase;
  • catalase;
  • reactive oxygen species;
  • cellular oxidative damage. Pasted text

These mechanisms remain research findings rather than proof that GHK-Cu treats inflammatory disease.

Angiogenesis and Tissue Remodelling

GHK-Cu has also been investigated for its influence on new blood-vessel formation and tissue remodelling.

Angiogenesis can support oxygen and nutrient delivery during tissue repair, while extracellular-matrix turnover contributes to structural organisation of damaged tissue. Pasted text

These pathways are particularly relevant to regenerative and wound-healing research.

Skin Ageing and Dermal Research

Human and laboratory research has examined GHK-Cu in relation to:

  • dermal density;
  • skin elasticity;
  • collagen matrix organisation;
  • fine-line and wrinkle appearance;
  • hydration;
  • tissue resilience. Pasted text

However, evidence from topical cosmetic formulations should not automatically be extrapolated to systemic administration.

Hair-Follicle Research

GHK-Cu has been studied in experimental hair-follicle models.

The supplied source describes research involving:

  • dermal papilla cells;
  • follicular activity;
  • anagen-phase biology;
  • vascular supply;
  • inflammatory signalling around follicles. Pasted text

This does not establish GHK-Cu as an approved treatment for hair loss.

Oxidative and Cellular Ageing Research

GHK-Cu is also investigated for potential cytoprotective activity.

Its copper-binding properties and influence on antioxidant pathways have generated interest in research involving oxidative stress, DNA damage, mitochondrial biology, and age-associated cellular changes. Pasted text

Claims of systemic anti-ageing effects remain unproven.

Fibrosis and Matrix-Regulation Research

The supplied material describes experimental findings involving TGF-β1 and other fibrosis-related pathways.

This has led to research into whether GHK-Cu may influence the balance between excessive scar formation and normal extracellular-matrix remodelling. Pasted text

Most of this research remains preclinical.

Gene-Expression Research

Transcriptomic research has explored broad changes in gene-expression patterns following exposure to GHK-Cu.

Reported pathways involve:

  • tissue repair;
  • antioxidant defence;
  • inflammation;
  • extracellular-matrix regulation;
  • cellular growth;
  • metabolism. Pasted text

GHRP-6 Pen

Product Description

GHRP-6 (Growth Hormone-Releasing Peptide-6) is a synthetic peptide and growth hormone secretagogue studied for its interaction with the growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHS-R1a).

GHRP-6 is part of the ghrelin-mimetic family. By activating GHS-R1a receptors within the hypothalamic and pituitary systems, it has been investigated for its ability to stimulate pulsatile endogenous growth hormone release while also influencing neural pathways involved in appetite and energy balance. Pasted text

Research areas include growth hormone and IGF-1 signalling, appetite regulation, metabolic signalling, endocrine function, recovery biology, and tissue-repair pathways.

Atlas Longevity GHRP-6 pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click cartridge system and are available in:

  • 5 mg GHRP-6
  • 10 mg GHRP-6

GHRP-6 remains an investigational peptide and should not be presented as an approved treatment for growth hormone deficiency, appetite disorders, muscle growth, recovery, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

GHRP-6 has been investigated in animal studies, laboratory research, and exploratory human research involving growth hormone secretion and endocrine signalling.

The supplied material describes the evidence base as primarily preclinical and exploratory, with limited human research. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material

Human observational research Limited

In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Human GH-response studies demonstrate biological activity, but this does not establish approved therapeutic efficacy or long-term safety.

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • healthy adult GH-response studies;
  • exploratory human endocrine research;
  • pediatric GH-related research;
  • rodent appetite models;
  • pituitary-cell studies;
  • aged animal models;
  • experimental cardiovascular research;
  • wound-healing animal models. Pasted text

The findings should be interpreted according to the specific study population and model.

Mechanism of Action

GHRP-6 acts primarily through the growth hormone secretagogue receptor GHS-R1a, a receptor also activated by the naturally occurring hormone ghrelin.

Receptor activation within the hypothalamus and pituitary can stimulate the release of endogenous growth hormone in pulses rather than supplying growth hormone directly.

Increased GH signalling can subsequently influence hepatic production of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) and downstream cellular pathways associated with protein synthesis, metabolism, and tissue biology. Pasted text

GHRP-6 is less selective than some other secretagogues. Experimental research indicates that it may also influence additional endocrine pathways, including ACTH, cortisol, prolactin, and appetite-related signalling.

This broader activity is an important distinction when interpreting GHRP-6 research.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Growth Hormone Secretion Research

GHRP-6 is primarily investigated for its ability to stimulate the body’s own growth hormone release.

Human and experimental studies have reported increases in circulating GH following GHRP-6 administration. The compound is therefore useful in research examining pituitary secretory responses and endogenous GH pulsatility. Pasted text

This does not establish GHRP-6 as an approved growth hormone treatment.

GH / IGF-1 Axis Research

Growth hormone can stimulate hepatic production of IGF-1, connecting GHRP-6 research with the broader GH–IGF-1 endocrine axis.

Experimental research examines downstream pathways involved in:

  • protein synthesis;
  • cellular growth;
  • connective-tissue biology;
  • metabolic regulation;
  • recovery signalling.

These mechanisms should not be translated into guaranteed muscle growth or recovery outcomes.

Appetite and Ghrelin Signalling

A major feature distinguishing GHRP-6 from more selective secretagogues is its effect on appetite-related neural signalling.

Because GHRP-6 mimics aspects of ghrelin receptor activation, animal and exploratory human research has examined its influence on hunger and food-intake signalling. Pasted text

This makes GHRP-6 relevant to research into the relationship between endocrine signalling, energy intake, and metabolic regulation.

Metabolic Research

Growth hormone and ghrelin systems both participate in energy metabolism.

GHRP-6 therefore provides an experimental model for studying interactions between:

  • GH secretion;
  • lipid metabolism;
  • nutrient utilisation;
  • appetite;
  • energy balance.

Its metabolic effects are complex because appetite stimulation can occur alongside GH-related metabolic signalling.

Recovery and Tissue Biology

Growth hormone and IGF-1 participate in pathways associated with cellular growth and tissue repair.

For this reason, GHRP-6 has been studied in experimental models involving recovery, connective tissue, collagen deposition, and wound healing. Pasted text

Animal recovery findings should not be interpreted as established human clinical benefits.

Hypothalamic-Pituitary Research

GHRP-6 is of particular interest because its activity involves both hypothalamic and pituitary signalling.

This makes it useful for research examining communication between central nervous system pathways and pituitary somatotroph cells involved in GH secretion. Pasted text

Broader Endocrine Signalling

Unlike highly selective GH secretagogues, GHRP-6 may affect additional hormone pathways.

Experimental models have reported effects involving:

  • ACTH;
  • cortisol;
  • prolactin;
  • GH;
  • IGF-1. Pasted text

This broader endocrine activity is scientifically relevant but also means GHRP-6 should not be described as affecting GH alone.

tabs.html:
Glow Blend 70 mg Pen

Product Description

Glow Blend is a multi-peptide research formulation combining BPC-157, TB-500, and GHK-Cu within a single regenerative research blend.

The three components are studied across different but potentially complementary biological pathways involving tissue repair, angiogenesis, cellular migration, collagen synthesis, extracellular-matrix regulation, inflammatory signalling, and antioxidant defence. Pasted text

Rather than relying on a single mechanism, Glow Blend is designed as a multi-pathway research formulation:

  • BPC-157 is associated primarily with angiogenesis, fibroblast activity, nitric-oxide signalling, and experimental connective-tissue repair.
  • TB-500-related research focuses on actin-associated cellular migration, wound repair, and tissue remodelling.
  • GHK-Cu is studied extensively for collagen production, extracellular-matrix biology, antioxidant activity, and dermal regeneration.

The Atlas Longevity Glow Blend pen contains 70 mg total blend in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

The exact amount of BPC-157, TB-500, and GHK-Cu within that 70 mg total was not supplied in the reference material, so individual component concentrations should not be invented.

Glow Blend remains an investigational research formulation and should not be presented as an approved treatment for injury, skin ageing, joint conditions, wound healing, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The exact Glow Blend formulation has a substantially weaker evidence base than the individual compounds contained within it.

The supplied material identifies the overall blend as a research formulation and does not provide evidence of regulatory therapeutic approval. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized trials of exact blend Not established
Observational evidence Limited / referenced
Animal research Yes, primarily involving individual components
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

An important distinction is that evidence involving BPC-157, TB-500, or GHK-Cu individually does not automatically prove that the exact three-component Glow Blend has the same clinical effects.

Evidence Type

The supplied research material includes:

  • tendon and connective-tissue models involving BPC-157;
  • muscle and cellular-migration research involving TB-500-related pathways;
  • human fibroblast and dermal research involving GHK-Cu;
  • in-vitro angiogenesis and wound-closure models;
  • rodent wound-healing research;
  • oxidative-stress assays;
  • experimental ageing-skin models. Pasted text

Most of the evidence concerns the individual components or related biological pathways, rather than controlled human trials of the exact combined formulation.

Mechanism of Action

Glow Blend is designed around three complementary research pathways.

BPC-157-Related Pathways

BPC-157 is studied for its potential influence on:

  • VEGF signalling;
  • angiogenesis;
  • FAK-paxillin pathways;
  • fibroblast migration;
  • nitric-oxide regulation;
  • tissue-repair signalling.

TB-500-Related Pathways

TB-500-related research focuses on thymosin beta-4-associated mechanisms involving:

  • actin binding;
  • cell migration;
  • cytoskeletal organisation;
  • tissue re-epithelialisation;
  • regenerative signalling;
  • inflammatory modulation.

GHK-Cu-Related Pathways

GHK-Cu is studied for:

  • collagen synthesis;
  • extracellular-matrix gene expression;
  • copper-dependent antioxidant activity;
  • fibroblast function;
  • angiogenesis;
  • tissue remodelling.

The supplied reference describes the blend as combining vascular, cytoskeletal, and extracellular-matrix mechanisms within a single regenerative research model. Pasted text

However, mechanistic complementarity should not be interpreted as proof that the combination is clinically synergistic in humans.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Multi-Pathway Tissue-Regeneration Research

Glow Blend is primarily designed for research investigating several repair pathways simultaneously.

BPC-157, TB-500, and GHK-Cu are associated with different aspects of tissue biology, including cellular migration, angiogenesis, fibroblast activity, collagen organisation, and extracellular-matrix remodelling. Pasted text

The proposed advantage is experimental breadth rather than a proven clinical superiority over individual compounds.

Wound-Healing Research

The component peptides have each been investigated in models relevant to wound repair.

Research areas include:

  • fibroblast migration;
  • epithelial repair;
  • collagen formation;
  • angiogenesis;
  • cellular migration;
  • extracellular-matrix organisation.

The supplied material describes faster wound closure and improved structural repair in experimental models, but these findings should not be presented as established human outcomes. Pasted text

Collagen and Dermal Research

GHK-Cu contributes much of the blend’s research relevance to skin and extracellular-matrix biology.

Experimental research includes collagen, elastin, glycosaminoglycans, fibroblast activity, dermal structure, and tissue remodelling.

BPC-157 and TB-500-related pathways may provide additional experimental interest through cellular migration and vascular signalling. Pasted text

Claims such as visibly younger skin or wrinkle reversal should not be treated as guaranteed outcomes of an injectable blend.

Angiogenesis and Microvascular Research

All three components have been discussed in relation to pathways affecting vascular repair or cellular migration.

Experimental research examines mechanisms including:

  • VEGF signalling;
  • endothelial activity;
  • new capillary formation;
  • microcirculation;
  • vascular tissue remodelling. Pasted text

These findings remain primarily mechanistic and preclinical.

Inflammation and Oxidative-Stress Research

The blend is also relevant to research involving the cellular environment surrounding tissue damage.

The supplied material describes changes involving:

  • TNF-α;
  • IL-6;
  • antioxidant-enzyme activity;
  • superoxide dismutase;
  • oxidative-stress markers. Pasted text

This should not be interpreted as proof that Glow Blend treats inflammatory disease.

Muscle, Tendon and Ligament Research

BPC-157 and TB-500-related research has focused heavily on experimental musculoskeletal repair.

Research areas include:

  • fibroblast activity;
  • muscle-cell migration;
  • connective-tissue repair;
  • tendon remodelling;
  • angiogenesis;
  • collagen-matrix organisation. Pasted text

GHK-Cu adds a separate extracellular-matrix and collagen-related mechanism to the research concept.

Human injury-recovery efficacy for the exact blend has not been established.

Skin and Extracellular-Matrix Biology

Glow Blend has also been positioned for dermal research because GHK-Cu has a substantial research history involving skin fibroblasts and extracellular-matrix proteins.

The supplied source discusses experimental effects involving skin structure, elasticity, collagen, and dermal repair. Pasted text

Evidence from topical or cellular GHK-Cu research should not automatically be extrapolated to injectable Glow Blend use.

Neural and Vascular Repair Research

BPC-157 and thymosin-related research includes experimental neurological and vascular injury models.

The source therefore discusses Glow Blend in relation to neurovascular repair, although these findings are predominantly based on individual component research rather than clinical studies of the blend itself. Pasted text

Joint and Connective-Tissue Research

The blend is also of research interest in models examining:

  • collagen organisation;
  • cartilage-associated pathways;
  • connective-tissue integrity;
  • fibrosis;
  • tissue flexibility.

The supplied material discusses these areas, but it does not establish Glow Blend as an approved treatment for arthritis, cartilage injury, or joint pain. Pasted text

Cellular Ageing Research

GHK-Cu-related gene-expression and antioxidant research has led to broader interest in cellular ageing and repair.

Within Glow Blend, these pathways are combined conceptually with the regenerative mechanisms associated with BPC-157 and TB-500. Pasted text

Terms such as “anti-ageing” or “rejuvenation” should therefore be understood as research categories rather than established therapeutic outcomes.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
BPC-157 tendon injury models Increased fibroblast migration and repair-related activity
TB-500-related muscle repair research Increased cellular migration and actin-associated repair signalling
GHK-Cu human fibroblast cultures Increased collagen synthesis and extracellular-matrix gene expression
Combined in-vitro peptide models Increased angiogenic signalling and changes in wound closure
Rodent wound-healing models Increased epithelialisation and capillary density
Oxidative-stress assays Reduced lipid-peroxidation markers and increased antioxidant-enzyme activity
Experimental ageing-skin models Changes in dermal thickness, wrinkle-related measures and antioxidant markers

The table combines evidence involving individual components with limited combination research. It should therefore not be read as evidence that every finding has been demonstrated using the exact Atlas Glow Blend formulation. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

Glow Blend already combines three compounds within one formulation:

BPC-157 + TB-500 + GHK-Cu

The supplied source additionally mentions experimental research concepts involving NAD+ or SS-31 alongside the blend. Pasted text

However, adequate combination-specific human evidence is not supplied.

Atlas Longevity therefore does not present additional combinations as validated or recommended protocols.
