The source-referenced amounts do not establish an approved human dosage, treatment frequency, treatment duration, or clinical protocol.

Possible Side Effects

The supplied source gives a relatively detailed adverse-effect list for Glow Blend, but several of its frequency and safety claims are not supported by study details in the material provided.

For example, the source states a specific percentage for injection-site reactions but does not provide sufficient supporting trial information to validate that incidence rate. For that reason, Atlas Longevity should not reproduce that percentage as an established risk estimate. Pasted text

Effects described in the supplied material include:

  • localized redness;
  • swelling;
  • itching or discomfort;
  • temporary skin discoloration associated with the copper-containing component;
  • nausea or gastrointestinal changes;
  • fatigue;
  • headache;
  • joint stiffness;
  • changes in sleep patterns;
  • metallic taste or temporary pigmentation changes;
  • hypersensitivity-type reactions.

These should not be interpreted as a complete or clinically established adverse-effect profile.

Because this is a multi-component formulation, important uncertainties remain regarding:

  • long-term systemic safety;
  • component interactions;
  • allergic or hypersensitivity responses;
  • copper-related effects;
  • medication interactions;
  • contraindications;
  • reproductive risks;
  • repeated systemic exposure.

The safety profile of each individual component cannot simply be added together to prove the safety of the combined product.

The reference source provides refrigeration and stability specifications for its own pre-mixed product, but those conditions should not automatically be transferred to Atlas Longevity without formulation-specific stability evidence.

This is particularly important for a multi-component formulation because stability requirements may depend on the concentrations, excipients, pH, and interaction of the individual peptides within the finished product.

Follow the temperature requirements, handling guidance, light-protection instructions, and shelf-life information shown on the Atlas Longevity product label or accompanying documentation.

Glutathione 1500 mg Pen

Product Description

Glutathione (GSH) is a naturally occurring tripeptide composed of glutamate, cysteine, and glycine and is one of the body’s key intracellular antioxidant systems.

It plays a central role in redox regulation, detoxification pathways, oxidative-stress defence, mitochondrial protection, and cellular homeostasis. Research has also examined glutathione in relation to liver metabolism, immune function, cellular ageing, and skin-pigmentation biology. Pasted text

tabs.title: Description
tabs.html:
IGF-1 LR3 1 mg Pen

Product Description

IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1) is a modified analogue of IGF-1 developed for research into IGF-1 receptor signalling, cellular growth, muscle biology, metabolic regulation, and tissue-repair pathways.

Compared with native IGF-1, IGF-1 LR3 has structural modifications designed to reduce its interaction with certain IGF-binding proteins and extend its biological activity. This makes it useful in experimental models where researchers require more prolonged IGF-1 receptor engagement. Pasted text

Unlike growth hormone secretagogues that act upstream through the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, IGF-1 LR3 acts more directly at IGF-1 receptors on peripheral tissues, activating intracellular pathways associated with protein synthesis, cellular survival, glucose handling, and structural adaptation.

The Atlas Longevity IGF-1 LR3 pen contains 1 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

IGF-1 LR3 remains an investigational compound. It should not be presented as an approved treatment for muscle growth, recovery, metabolic conditions, anti-ageing, or other medical purposes.

Clinical / Research Status

IGF-1 biology has been investigated extensively, but evidence for the Long R3 analogue itself is considerably more limited than evidence concerning native IGF-1.

The supplied material characterizes IGF-1 LR3 research as primarily preclinical and exploratory, with limited human data. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research specific to IGF-1 LR3 Limited / exploratory
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Research into native IGF-1 or the broader IGF signalling system should not automatically be treated as clinical evidence for IGF-1 LR3.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • skeletal-muscle animal models;
  • myoblast cell cultures;
  • IGF-1 receptor signalling;
  • pharmacokinetic comparison with native IGF-1;
  • satellite-cell and cellular-repair models;
  • glucose-metabolism studies;
  • intracellular anabolic signalling assays. Pasted text

Most of the specific evidence presented for IGF-1 LR3 is therefore animal or in-vitro evidence, rather than large controlled human clinical trials.

Mechanism of Action

IGF-1 LR3 acts primarily through the IGF-1 receptor (IGF-1R), a receptor tyrosine kinase expressed across many tissues.

When IGF-1R is activated, it can trigger several intracellular signalling networks, particularly:

  • PI3K
  • Akt
  • mTOR
  • MAPK-related pathways

These pathways regulate cellular growth, protein synthesis, survival, nutrient utilisation, and tissue adaptation. Pasted text

Extended Activity

A defining feature of IGF-1 LR3 is reduced affinity for several IGF-binding proteins compared with native IGF-1.

The supplied reference describes this as contributing to greater availability of unbound peptide and more prolonged receptor activity in experimental systems.

This extended activity distinguishes IGF-1 LR3 from shorter-acting native IGF-1.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

IGF-1 Receptor Signalling

IGF-1 LR3 is researched primarily as a direct activator of IGF-1R.

This receptor is involved in:

  • cellular growth;
  • protein synthesis;
  • metabolic regulation;
  • tissue development;
  • cell-survival signalling.

Because IGF-1 LR3 acts at the receptor level, its research profile differs from peptides that first stimulate growth hormone release through the pituitary. Pasted text

Protein-Synthesis Research

Activation of IGF-1R can stimulate the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway, one of the major intracellular systems involved in protein synthesis and cellular growth.

For this reason, IGF-1 LR3 is studied in models examining skeletal-muscle adaptation and anabolic signalling. Pasted text

These mechanisms should not be interpreted as guaranteed muscle gain in humans.

Muscle-Cell and Satellite-Cell Research

IGF signalling contributes to the biology of satellite cells, which are precursor cells involved in skeletal-muscle repair and adaptation.

Experimental models have investigated whether IGF-1-related signalling can influence:

  • satellite-cell activation;
  • myoblast proliferation;
  • cellular differentiation;
  • muscle-fibre development. Pasted text

Human performance outcomes for IGF-1 LR3 are not established by these laboratory findings.

Cellular Survival Research

Akt signalling downstream of IGF-1R can interact with cellular survival pathways and reduce certain apoptotic signals under experimental conditions.

This has created interest in IGF-1 LR3 for broader tissue-repair and cellular-resilience research. Pasted text

Because promoting cellular survival and proliferation can also carry biological risks, this mechanism should not automatically be framed as universally beneficial.

Glucose and Metabolic Signalling

IGF-1 shares structural and signalling similarities with insulin.

IGF-1 receptor activation can therefore influence:

  • peripheral glucose uptake;
  • nutrient utilisation;
  • energy partitioning;
  • insulin-related metabolic pathways. Pasted text

This mechanism is particularly important from a safety perspective because excessive IGF-like activity can affect blood-glucose regulation.

Downstream Endocrine Research

Unlike GHRH analogues or growth hormone secretagogues, IGF-1 LR3 does not rely on stimulating pituitary GH release first.

It acts further downstream within the growth-signalling system by directly activating peripheral IGF-1 receptors. Pasted text

This distinction makes it relevant to studies specifically examining receptor-level anabolic signalling rather than upstream endocrine stimulation.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Rodent skeletal-muscle model Increased myofibre hypertrophy and protein-synthesis signalling
In-vitro myoblast culture Increased proliferation and differentiation with enhanced Akt/mTOR signalling
Pharmacokinetic comparison Longer biological activity and reduced IGF-binding protein affinity compared with native IGF-1
Cellular-repair models Increased satellite-cell activation and regeneration-related markers
Glucose-metabolism studies Increased peripheral glucose uptake and altered insulin-related signalling
Anabolic signalling assays Prolonged IGF-1 receptor phosphorylation and downstream PI3K activity

These findings are primarily preclinical and mechanistic and should not be represented as established human clinical outcomes. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied reference discusses experimental combinations involving IGF-1 LR3 with:

  • CJC-1295;
  • Ipamorelin;
  • BPC-157;
  • TB-500. Pasted text

The theoretical research rationale involves combining direct IGF-1 receptor signalling with upstream growth hormone signalling or tissue-repair pathways.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

Because IGF-1 LR3 can influence glucose metabolism and cellular proliferation, combination research should not be presented as automatically safe or beneficial.

Possible Side Effects

IGF-1 LR3 requires particularly cautious safety framing because IGF signalling affects glucose regulation, cellular growth, and proliferative pathways.

The supplied material reports possible effects including:

  • hypoglycaemia / low blood glucose related to insulin-like metabolic activity;
  • injection-site swelling, redness, or discomfort;
  • headache;
  • lightheadedness;
  • joint discomfort;
  • muscle cramps;
  • organ-growth effects observed with prolonged high exposure in animal models. Pasted text

Glucose-Related Risk

Because IGF signalling can increase peripheral glucose uptake, low blood glucose is a biologically plausible and important concern.

Symptoms associated with hypoglycaemia can become serious and should not be minimized as a routine or harmless research effect.

Cellular-Proliferation Considerations

IGF-1 receptor activation promotes cell survival and growth signalling.

That mechanism is valuable experimentally but also creates legitimate scientific concern regarding inappropriate cellular proliferation.

The source itself notes that long-term effects involving cellular proliferation remain under investigation. Pasted text

  • long-term systemic safety;
  • tumour-related risk;

  • contraindications;

Kisspeptin 10 mg Pen

Product Description

Kisspeptin, commonly studied as Kisspeptin-10 (KP-10), is a neuropeptide involved in regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis, one of the body’s central reproductive endocrine systems.

Kisspeptin acts upstream in this pathway by stimulating hypothalamic neurons responsible for releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). GnRH subsequently signals the pituitary gland to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which regulate downstream reproductive hormone activity.

Human and animal research has examined kisspeptin in relation to reproductive endocrinology, gonadotropin secretion, testosterone signalling, ovulatory physiology, fertility pathways, and neurobiological processes associated with sexual behaviour. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity Kisspeptin pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Kisspeptin remains an investigational research compound and should not be presented as an approved treatment for infertility, hypogonadism, low testosterone, libido disorders, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

Kisspeptin has a stronger human research base than many experimental peptides.

The supplied material identifies:

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material

Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

The reference describes controlled human studies examining HPG-axis activation, gonadotropin release, reproductive endocrinology, and related neuroendocrine responses. Pasted text

However, clinical investigation does not automatically mean that Kisspeptin-10 is approved for routine therapeutic use.

Evidence Type

The supplied research includes:

  • healthy male volunteer studies;
  • reproductive-endocrinology studies;
  • research involving hypogonadotropic hypogonadism;
  • studies involving hypothalamic amenorrhea;
  • IVF-related investigations;
  • functional MRI research;
  • animal hypothalamic models;
  • puberty and reproductive-development models. Pasted text

Evidence quality differs depending on population, formulation, administration method, and research endpoint.

Mechanism of Action

Kisspeptin acts primarily through the KISS1 receptor (KISS1R / GPR54).

Activation of KISS1R on hypothalamic GnRH neurons can stimulate the release of GnRH.

This initiates a hormonal cascade:

Kisspeptin → GnRH → LH / FSH → downstream reproductive hormone signalling

LH and FSH then act on the gonads and influence reproductive processes including testosterone production, estrogen signalling, follicular development, and ovulatory physiology. Pasted text

Because kisspeptin works near the top of this endocrine hierarchy, it is particularly useful in research focused on upstream neuroendocrine regulation rather than direct hormone replacement.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

HPG-Axis Activation Research

Kisspeptin is one of the key regulatory signals controlling the reproductive endocrine axis.

Its ability to activate GnRH neurons makes it useful for studying how hypothalamic signals influence pituitary and gonadal hormone production.

This upstream mechanism distinguishes kisspeptin from compounds that directly supply testosterone, estrogen, or other downstream hormones. Pasted text

LH and Testosterone Research

Human studies described in the supplied material have investigated whether kisspeptin can increase LH secretion in male research participants.

Because LH stimulates Leydig cells in the testes, increased LH can subsequently influence endogenous testosterone production. Pasted text

This does not establish Kisspeptin as an approved testosterone-replacement therapy.

Female Reproductive and Ovulatory Research

Kisspeptin plays an important role in the neuroendocrine signalling involved in the LH surge associated with ovulation.

Clinical research has therefore examined kisspeptin in fertility and reproductive-medicine settings, including studies involving oocyte maturation and hypothalamic reproductive dysfunction. Pasted text

Results from these controlled research settings should not be interpreted as general fertility-treatment guidance.

Libido and Neurobiological Research

Kisspeptin research extends beyond hormone concentrations.

Human functional imaging studies described in the source have examined its influence on brain regions involved in emotional, motivational, and sexual processing. Pasted text

This makes kisspeptin relevant to research examining the interaction between reproductive hormones and central nervous system signalling.

It does not establish kisspeptin as an approved libido-enhancing treatment.

Endocrine Feedback Research

Because kisspeptin stimulates the body’s own upstream reproductive signalling, researchers can study the HPG axis while preserving much of the normal endocrine cascade.

This makes it useful for investigating:

  • GnRH responses;
  • LH and FSH secretion;
  • gonadal hormone signalling;
  • hypothalamic-pituitary feedback;
  • pulsatile endocrine activity. Pasted text

Hypogonadism Research

Kisspeptin has also been examined in populations with abnormalities affecting reproductive hormone signalling.

The supplied material describes studies reporting gonadotropin responses in certain forms of hypogonadotropic endocrine dysfunction. Pasted text

This remains specialist research and should not be represented as a broadly established treatment for low testosterone or hypogonadism.

tabs.html:
Klow Blend 80 mg Pen

Product Description

Klow Blend is a multi-peptide research formulation combining BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu, and KPV within a single regenerative research blend.

The formulation expands on multi-pathway peptide research by combining compounds associated with angiogenesis, fibroblast activity, extracellular-matrix regulation, collagen synthesis, cellular migration, inflammatory signalling, oxidative-stress pathways, and tissue remodelling. Pasted text

Within the supplied research framework:

  • BPC-157 is associated with VEGF, nitric-oxide signalling, fibroblast activity, and experimental tissue repair.
  • TB-500-related research focuses on actin-associated cellular migration and endothelial or tissue-remodelling pathways.
  • GHK-Cu is studied for collagen, elastin, extracellular-matrix regulation, and antioxidant-related activity.
  • KPV is described in the source in relation to inflammatory, vascular-permeability, oxidative-stress, and cellular-support pathways.

The Atlas Longevity Klow Blend pen contains 80 mg total blend in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

The supplied material does not state how the 80 mg total is divided between BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu, and KPV. Individual component concentrations must therefore not be invented.

Klow Blend remains an investigational multi-peptide formulation and should not be presented as an approved treatment for injury, inflammation, skin ageing, joint disorders, neurological conditions, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The exact four-component Klow Blend formulation has a substantially more limited evidence base than the individual compounds from which it is constructed.

The supplied material identifies the formulation as intended for experimental research and does not establish therapeutic approval. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized trials of exact Klow Blend Not established
Human observational evidence Limited / indirect
Animal research Yes, primarily component-based
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Evidence involving BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu, or KPV individually should not automatically be treated as proof of safety or effectiveness for the exact four-component formulation.

Evidence Type

The supplied material references research involving:

  • BPC-157 muscle and connective-tissue models;
  • TB-500-related tendon and cellular-migration research;
  • GHK-Cu fibroblast and skin-regeneration studies;
  • KPV endothelial and inflammatory models;
  • combined peptide models;
  • rodent dermal wound research;
  • experimental ageing-skin assays. Pasted text

Most of the evidence therefore relates to individual ingredients or preclinical models, rather than controlled clinical investigation of the final Klow Blend.

Mechanism of Action

Klow Blend is designed around four complementary research pathways.

BPC-157-Related Pathways

The supplied material describes BPC-157 in relation to:

  • VEGF signalling;
  • nitric-oxide regulation;
  • angiogenesis;
  • fibroblast activity;
  • extracellular-matrix deposition.

TB-500-Related Pathways

TB-500-related research is described in connection with:

  • actin modulation;
  • cellular migration;
  • endothelial repair;
  • tissue re-epithelialisation;
  • cytoskeletal organisation.

GHK-Cu-Related Pathways

GHK-Cu is associated with:

  • collagen synthesis;
  • elastin;
  • glycosaminoglycans;
  • extracellular-matrix turnover;
  • TGF-β / SMAD-related signalling;
  • antioxidant pathways.

KPV-Related Pathways

Within the supplied source, KPV is described in relation to:

  • cytokine regulation;
  • vascular permeability;
  • inflammatory signalling;
  • oxidative-stress control;
  • tissue-environment regulation.

The source presents these four mechanisms as a multi-pathway regenerative framework. Pasted text

Mechanistic complementarity does not by itself establish clinically meaningful synergy in humans.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Multi-Pathway Regeneration Research

Klow Blend combines four compounds associated with different aspects of tissue biology.

The proposed research concept involves simultaneous investigation of:

  • tissue repair;
  • angiogenesis;
  • collagen synthesis;
  • cellular migration;
  • inflammation;
  • oxidative stress;
  • extracellular-matrix remodelling. Pasted text

The supplied material describes this as a more comprehensive research formulation, but comparative superiority over other formulations has not been clinically established.

Muscle, Tendon and Ligament Research

BPC-157 and TB-500-related pathways form much of the blend’s musculoskeletal research rationale.

Experimental areas include:

  • fibroblast activity;
  • tissue migration;
  • angiogenesis;
  • tendon biology;
  • muscle-repair signalling;
  • connective-tissue organisation.

GHK-Cu contributes collagen-related pathways, while the source describes KPV as providing additional inflammatory and oxidative-stress modulation. Pasted text

Human injury-recovery efficacy for the complete formulation remains unestablished.

Collagen and Structural-Tissue Research

GHK-Cu is particularly relevant to collagen and extracellular-matrix biology.

The source discusses potential interaction between:

  • collagen formation;
  • elastin production;
  • actin organisation;
  • fibroblast activity;
  • tissue resilience. Pasted text

These remain research mechanisms rather than guaranteed clinical outcomes.

Wound-Healing and Skin-Regeneration Research

The supplied material positions Klow Blend within research involving:

  • epithelial repair;
  • angiogenesis;
  • fibroblast proliferation;
  • collagen formation;
  • dermal density;
  • oxidative-stress regulation. Pasted text

Findings from individual peptide studies should not be represented as proof that the complete injectable blend improves wound healing or skin appearance in humans.

Microcirculation and Vascular Research

The four components are discussed in relation to different aspects of vascular and tissue-perfusion biology.

Experimental pathways described in the source include:

  • VEGF;
  • endothelial migration;
  • capillary integrity;
  • angiogenesis;
  • nitric-oxide-related signalling. Pasted text

These mechanisms are predominantly preclinical.

Inflammatory and Oxidative-Stress Research

KPV, BPC-157, and GHK-Cu are described in the supplied material as influencing inflammatory or oxidative pathways.

Research areas include:

  • TNF-α;
  • IL-6;
  • CRP-related inflammatory markers;
  • antioxidant activity;
  • cellular oxidative stress. Pasted text

The supplied evidence does not establish Klow Blend as a treatment for inflammatory disease.

Joint and Connective-Tissue Research

The blend is also positioned for experimental research involving:

  • cartilage-associated pathways;
  • connective-tissue integrity;
  • collagen organisation;
  • fibrosis;
  • tissue flexibility. Pasted text

Claims of improved joint health, mobility, or cartilage repair should remain appropriately qualified.

Cellular Energy and Mitochondrial Research

The supplied source attributes mitochondrial-support and energy-related effects to KPV within the blend. Pasted text

These claims should be presented cautiously because the supplied material does not provide controlled human evidence demonstrating that the complete Klow Blend improves mitochondrial energy production.

Fibrosis and Scar-Related Research

Several components are discussed in relation to extracellular-matrix remodelling and fibrotic signalling.

The supplied source describes pathways involving:

  • TGF-β;
  • collagen organisation;
  • cellular migration;
  • oxidative damage;
  • scar-related tissue remodelling. Pasted text

This remains an experimental research area.

Skin and Dermal Research

The source describes Klow Blend in relation to skin texture, hydration, elasticity, vascular support, and extracellular-matrix biology. Pasted text

Much of this rationale derives from GHK-Cu and component-level evidence rather than clinical testing of the entire formulation.

Neuroregeneration Research

The supplied material also discusses neuroprotective and neural-repair concepts based primarily on component-specific research. Pasted text

The exact Klow Blend has not been established as a treatment for neurological disease, cognitive decline, or nervous-system injury.

Ageing and Longevity Research

Klow Blend is positioned in the supplied material for research into:

  • oxidative stress;
  • inflammation;
  • extracellular-matrix changes;
  • tissue regeneration;
  • cellular ageing;
  • energy-related pathways. Pasted text

Terms such as “anti-ageing,” “rejuvenation,” or “longevity” should be treated as research categories rather than proven human outcomes.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
BPC-157 muscle-injury models Increased repair activity, capillary density and changes in inflammatory markers
TB-500-related tendon models Increased cellular migration, actin reorganisation and angiogenic activity
GHK-Cu human fibroblast models Increased collagen I/III and elastin-related expression
KPV endothelial models Changes in vascular permeability, oxidative stress and nitric-oxide-related signalling
Combined peptide models Changes in extracellular-matrix remodelling and angiogenic-factor expression
Rodent dermal wound models Increased epithelialisation with changes in fibrosis and antioxidant markers

These findings do not demonstrate that every outcome has been established using the exact Atlas Longevity Klow Blend formulation. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

Klow Blend already contains four research compounds:

BPC-157 + TB-500 + GHK-Cu + KPV

The supplied source additionally discusses experimental concepts involving:

  • NAD+;
  • SS-31. Pasted text

The proposed rationale involves redox biology and mitochondrial pathways.

However, the supplied material does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

Atlas Longevity therefore does not present additional combinations as recommended stacks.

but it does not state the individual milligram amount of each compound within the 80 mg total formulation.

For this reason, the calculations below show total Klow Blend amount only.

Protocol / Dosage Information

The supplied source describes experimental total quantities of:

within its proposed research protocols. Pasted text

The source’s original click calculations were based on a different 2 mL formulation and therefore do not apply to the Atlas Longevity pen.

Because the ingredient ratio is not supplied, it is not possible to state accurately how much BPC-157, TB-500, GHK-Cu, or KPV is present at 15 or 30 clicks.

The supplied source does not establish an approved human dosage, treatment schedule, cycle length, frequency, or clinical protocol for Klow Blend.

Possible Side Effects

The supplied material describes several effects that may occur in experimental research involving the blend.

Reported or proposed effects include:

  • localized redness;
  • swelling;
  • nausea or gastrointestinal discomfort;
  • temporary fatigue;
  • rash or hypersensitivity-type responses;
  • temporary joint discomfort;
  • pigmentation changes. Pasted text

The reference describes many of these effects as transient, but the exact blend does not have a sufficiently established human safety database to guarantee that adverse effects will be mild or temporary.

Important areas of uncertainty include:

  • long-term systemic exposure;
  • interaction between all four components;
  • copper-related effects from GHK-Cu;
  • hypersensitivity;
  • gastrointestinal effects;
  • medication interactions;
  • contraindications;
  • reproductive effects;
  • repeated exposure;
  • combination protocols.

Safety data for individual peptides should not simply be combined to claim that the final four-component formulation is safe.

The reference product provides refrigeration and stability specifications for its own pre-mixed product. Those claims should not automatically be transferred to Atlas Longevity without formulation-specific stability evidence.

This is especially important for a four-component formulation because stability may depend on individual peptide concentrations, excipients, pH, temperature, light exposure, and interactions within the finished formulation.

Follow the temperature requirements, handling guidance, light-protection instructions, and shelf-life information provided on the Atlas Longevity product label or accompanying documentation.

The source’s statement of 80 mg as “molecular weight” should not be carried into Atlas content because 80 mg represents the quantity of blend in the pen, not the molecular weight of a defined molecule.

HMG 75IU Bali

 

HMG 75IU, also known as Human Menopausal Gonadotropin or menotropins, is a gonadotropin preparation containing follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) activity.

Gonadotropins play important roles within the reproductive endocrine system, which is why HMG has been extensively studied and clinically used within fertility medicine.

Atlas Longevity supplies HMG 75IU with premium service and fast, discreet delivery throughout Bali.

 

What Is HMG?

HMG stands for Human Menopausal Gonadotropin.

It contains gonadotropin activity involving:

• FSH – Follicle-Stimulating Hormone
• LH – Luteinizing Hormone

These hormones are involved in reproductive function in both men and women.

 

Research & Clinical Areas

HMG/menotropins have been studied and used within areas including:

• Reproductive endocrinology
• Fertility medicine
• Follicular development
• Ovulation induction
• Spermatogenesis
• Gonadotropin signalling
• FSH and LH activity

HMG is a biologically active hormone product and should only be used under appropriate professional medical guidance where intended for clinical use.

 

HMG vs HCG

HMG and HCG are different products.

HMG provides FSH and LH activity.

HCG primarily acts through the LH receptor and mimics LH activity.

Because of this difference, the two products have distinct roles within reproductive endocrinology and should not be considered interchangeable.

WHAT IS MELANOTAN I?

Melanotan I is a synthetic peptide analogue of the naturally occurring hormone α-MSH — alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone.

It is primarily researched for its interaction with the melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R).

MC1R signalling plays an important role in pathways associated with melanin production and pigmentation.

Melanotan I is also frequently referred to as Melanotan-1 and is closely associated with the pharmaceutical compound afamelanotide.

MELANOTAN I RESEARCH AREAS

✔ Melanocortin receptor signalling

✔ Photobiology research

These areas relate to scientific investigation and should not be interpreted as claims that this research product diagnoses, treats or prevents any medical condition.

MELANOTAN I VS MELANOTAN II

Although their names are similar, Melanotan I and Melanotan II are different peptides.

Melanotan I

Melanotan I is primarily associated with MC1R signalling and pigmentation research.

It is generally considered more selective toward melanocortin pathways associated with pigmentation.

Melanotan II

Melanotan II interacts with a broader range of melanocortin receptors and is therefore researched across additional physiological pathways.

Mazdutide 10mg Bali – Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Peptide

 

What Is Mazdutide?

Mazdutide is a peptide-based dual receptor agonist that targets both glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon receptors.

It has been investigated in clinical studies involving obesity, body weight, appetite regulation and metabolic outcomes.

Unlike single-receptor GLP-1 medicines, mazdutide combines GLP-1 receptor activity with glucagon receptor activation.

How Does Mazdutide Work?

Mazdutide acts on two hormonal pathways:

GLP-1 Receptor

GLP-1 receptor activation is associated with appetite regulation, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and gastrointestinal effects.

Glucagon Receptor

Glucagon receptor activation influences hepatic glucose metabolism and energy-related biological pathways.

The combination is being studied for its effects on body weight and metabolic regulation.

Mazdutide Research Areas

Clinical research has investigated mazdutide in relation to:

  • Body-weight reduction
  • Appetite and food-intake regulation
  • Obesity management
  • Blood glucose regulation
  • Cardiometabolic risk factors
  • Liver-related metabolic measurements
  • Dual incretin and glucagon receptor signalling

Research findings depend on the population, study design, formulation and dose investigated. They do not establish the safety or efficacy of an independently supplied vial.

Semaglutide GLP-1
Tirzepatide GLP-1 + GIP
Retatrutide GLP-1 + GIP + Glucagon

These compounds have different clinical evidence, regulatory statuses and safety profiles. They are not interchangeable.

Melatonin: A naturally occurring hormone involved in circadian rhythm and sleep-wake regulation.

DSIP: An experimental neuropeptide historically investigated for possible relationships with sleep regulation.

Melatonin and DSIP are different compounds with distinct biological mechanisms and levels of supporting evidence.

What Is Survodutide?

Survodutide is a dual GCGR/GLP-1 receptor agonist.

Researchers are investigating whether targeting both pathways can provide complementary metabolic effects.

GLP-1 SMA:

tabs.html:
Melanotan I 10 mg Pen

Product Description

Melanotan I, also known as Afamelanotide, MT-I, or NDP-MSH, is a synthetic analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) developed for research into melanocortin signalling, pigmentation biology, melanogenesis, and photoprotection.

Its primary research target is the melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R) expressed on melanocytes. Activation of MC1R stimulates intracellular signalling involved in the production of eumelanin, the darker melanin pigment associated with skin pigmentation and natural photoprotective responses.

Compared with broader melanocortin agonists, Melanotan I is described in the supplied material as having greater selectivity toward pigmentation-related MC1R pathways. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity Melanotan I pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Afamelanotide has been clinically studied and has regulatory approval in certain jurisdictions for specific photoprotection indications. However, that regulatory status applies to specific approved formulations and indications and should not be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity pre-mixed pen or of Melanotan I for cosmetic tanning.

Clinical / Research Status

Melanotan I / Afamelanotide has a more developed human evidence base than many experimental peptides.

The supplied material identifies:

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory approval Yes, for specific indications/formulations in certain jurisdictions

The source specifically notes clinical evaluation and approval for certain photoprotection indications. Pasted text

This distinction is important:

Approval of an Afamelanotide medicinal product does not automatically mean that every Melanotan I formulation, injection pen, concentration, or use is approved.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • erythropoietic protoporphyria clinical trials;
  • healthy human pigmentation studies;
  • vitiligo combination studies;
  • melanocyte cell cultures;
  • UV-exposure animal models;
  • photosensitivity research;
  • pharmacokinetic studies involving an implant formulation. Pasted text

Evidence should always be interpreted according to the specific formulation and indication studied.

Mechanism of Action

Melanotan I acts primarily as an agonist of the melanocortin-1 receptor (MC1R).

MC1R is expressed on melanocytes, the cells responsible for producing melanin.

When MC1R is activated, intracellular signalling involving cyclic AMP (cAMP) increases. This signalling can influence:

  • MITF-related transcription;
  • tyrosinase activity;
  • melanogenesis;
  • eumelanin production;
  • pigmentation responses.

The supplied material describes Melanotan I as a more stable analogue of endogenous α-MSH with greater resistance to enzymatic breakdown and more sustained receptor engagement. Pasted text

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

MC1R Signalling Research

Melanotan I is primarily studied for selective activation of MC1R receptors.

These receptors regulate melanocyte signalling pathways involved in skin pigmentation and eumelanin synthesis.

Because Melanotan I is described as relatively selective for MC1R, it is particularly relevant to focused research involving pigmentation rather than broader melanocortin-system activity. Pasted text

Eumelanin Production Research

Activation of MC1R can increase cAMP signalling and stimulate pathways involved in melanin production.

The supplied material specifically describes:

  • increased MITF signalling;
  • increased tyrosinase-related activity;
  • increased eumelanin production. Pasted text

These mechanisms form the main scientific basis for Melanotan I pigmentation research.

Photoprotection Research

Melanin absorbs and dissipates part of the energy associated with ultraviolet exposure.

For this reason, increased eumelanin production has been investigated in research examining photoprotection and UV-response biology.

The supplied source describes human research involving EPP and experimental models examining UV-associated skin responses. Pasted text

This should not be interpreted as meaning Melanotan I replaces sunscreen, protective clothing, or other established UV-protection measures.

Stability Compared With Natural α-MSH

Natural α-MSH is rapidly degraded.

Melanotan I contains structural modifications intended to improve peptide stability and prolong interaction with melanocortin receptors.

This makes it more suitable for controlled research than native α-MSH in certain experimental settings. Pasted text

Dermatological Research

Melanotan I / Afamelanotide has been investigated in several dermatological research areas, including:

  • photosensitivity;
  • pigmentation biology;
  • EPP;
  • vitiligo-related repigmentation;
  • UV-response pathways.

The supplied material describes controlled human research in some of these areas. Pasted text

Results from specialist dermatological indications should not automatically be converted into cosmetic tanning claims.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Erythropoietic protoporphyria clinical trials Increased pain-free light exposure and improved photoprotection associated with increased eumelanin
Healthy human volunteer research Increased skin pigmentation following repeated administration
Vitiligo combination studies More rapid or uniform repigmentation when studied with NB-UVB
In-vitro melanocyte cultures Increased tyrosinase activity and eumelanin production through MC1R/cAMP signalling
UV-exposure animal models Reduced photodamage markers and altered erythema responses
Photosensitivity research Changes in phototoxic skin responses
Implant pharmacokinetic research Sustained melanocortin activity associated with a long-acting implant formulation

The research includes strong human evidence for specific medical and photobiological contexts, but findings from approved implant formulations should not automatically be applied to an Atlas Longevity pre-mixed pen. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combination concepts involving Melanotan I with:

  • GHK-Cu;
  • Glutathione;
  • BPC-157;
  • Epitalon. Pasted text

The proposed research rationale involves pigmentation, extracellular-matrix biology, antioxidant pathways, tissue repair, and ageing-related skin research.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be regarded as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

Possible Side Effects

The supplied material describes several adverse effects observed in Melanotan I / Afamelanotide research.

These include:

  • localized injection-site redness or irritation;
  • nausea;
  • temporary gastrointestinal discomfort;
  • headache;
  • mild fatigue;
  • facial flushing or warmth;
  • darkening of existing freckles;
  • darkening of existing nevi or moles. Pasted text

Pigmentation Changes

Because Melanotan I directly stimulates melanogenesis, pigmentation changes are expected to be a major biological effect.

This can include darkening of:

  • skin;
  • freckles;
  • existing pigmented lesions;
  • nevi.

Changes in existing moles or newly changing pigmented lesions should not be dismissed simply as an expected cosmetic effect.

Long-Term Safety

The supplied material describes a generally favorable safety profile within specific clinical contexts.

However, the evidence does not establish complete safety for:

  • cosmetic tanning use;
  • different injectable formulations;
  • prolonged unsupervised exposure;
  • repeated high exposure;
  • combination protocols;
  • individuals with dermatological risk factors.

Regulatory experience with an approved Afamelanotide product should not automatically be used to claim that every Melanotan I product or route has the same safety profile.

MC1R stands for melanocortin-1 receptor.

What is eumelanin?

NAD+ 500 mg / 1000 mg Pen

Product Description

NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) is an endogenous coenzyme central to cellular energy metabolism, redox reactions, mitochondrial respiration, and intracellular signalling.

NAD exists primarily in two interconvertible forms:

  • NAD+ — the oxidized form
  • NADH — the reduced form

Together, these molecules participate in electron-transfer reactions that help cells convert nutrients into usable energy through metabolic pathways including glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation.

NAD+ also serves as a substrate for enzymes including sirtuins and PARPs, connecting NAD biology with DNA repair, cellular stress responses, gene regulation, inflammation research, and mitochondrial function. Pasted text

Atlas Longevity NAD+ pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click cartridge system and are available in:

  • 500 mg NAD+
  • 1000 mg NAD+

NAD+ is naturally present in the body, but injectable NAD+ preparations remain investigational and should not be presented as approved treatments for ageing, fatigue, cognitive decline, metabolic disease, or other medical conditions. Pasted text

Clinical / Research Status

NAD biology has been studied extensively across human, animal, and cellular research.

However, there is an important distinction between research into:

  • endogenous NAD metabolism;
  • NAD+ itself;
  • NAD precursors such as NMN or NR;
  • intravenous NAD+;
  • other injectable NAD+ formulations.

The supplied material states that injectable and IV NAD+ preparations are used experimentally but are not approved for therapeutic purposes. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory approval for Atlas NAD+ pen Not established

Evidence involving NMN or nicotinamide riboside should not automatically be presented as direct evidence for an NAD+ injection pen.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • intravenous NAD+ administration;
  • human observational metabolic research;
  • animal ageing models;
  • cellular ageing models;
  • neuronal cell cultures;
  • metabolic-disease models;
  • exercise-related research;
  • brain-ischaemia experimental models. Pasted text

The clinical relevance of these studies varies substantially depending on formulation, route of administration, species, and research endpoint.

Mechanism of Action

NAD+ is a central participant in cellular oxidation-reduction reactions.

During energy metabolism, NAD+ accepts electrons and becomes NADH. NADH can then donate electrons within mitochondrial pathways involved in ATP generation.

The supplied material describes NAD+ involvement in:

  • glycolysis;
  • the TCA / Krebs cycle;
  • oxidative phosphorylation;
  • electron transport;
  • ATP generation;
  • PARP-mediated DNA repair;
  • sirtuin activity;
  • mitochondrial biogenesis;
  • stress-response signalling;
  • AMPK-associated pathways. Pasted text

Sirtuin Signalling

Sirtuins are NAD-dependent enzymes involved in metabolic regulation, gene expression, stress responses, and mitochondrial biology.

Because sirtuin activity requires NAD+, changes in cellular NAD availability may alter several downstream signalling systems.

PARP and DNA Repair

PARP enzymes also consume NAD+ during responses to DNA damage.

This relationship has generated substantial interest in NAD metabolism within research involving cellular ageing and genomic stability.

These mechanisms establish NAD+ as an essential biological molecule but do not by themselves prove that additional injectable NAD+ produces anti-ageing or disease-treatment effects.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Cellular Energy and ATP Research

NAD+ is essential for numerous redox reactions involved in cellular energy metabolism.

Research examines how NAD+/NADH balance affects:

  • mitochondrial respiration;
  • nutrient metabolism;
  • ATP generation;
  • cellular energy availability. Pasted text

This fundamental biological role should not be converted into guaranteed claims of increased energy following supplementation.

Mitochondrial Function

NAD+ plays an important role in oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial metabolism.

Experimental studies therefore investigate NAD-related pathways in:

  • mitochondrial function;
  • mitochondrial biogenesis;
  • oxidative metabolism;
  • cellular stress resilience. Pasted text

Sirtuin and Ageing Research

NAD+ is required by SIRT1–SIRT7 enzymes.

This has generated significant interest in research involving:

  • metabolic regulation;
  • gene expression;
  • mitochondrial signalling;
  • stress resistance;
  • cellular ageing. Pasted text

Animal lifespan findings involving NAD-related pathways do not establish that injectable NAD+ extends human lifespan.

DNA-Repair Research

NAD+ serves as a substrate for PARP enzymes involved in DNA-damage responses.

Researchers therefore study the relationship between NAD availability, PARP activity, DNA repair, genomic stability, and cellular stress. Pasted text

This does not establish NAD+ injection as a treatment for DNA damage or ageing.

Neurological and Brain-Energy Research

NAD-related pathways are also studied in neurons because the brain has substantial energy demands and is sensitive to mitochondrial dysfunction.

The source discusses experimental research involving:

  • neuronal metabolism;
  • oxidative stress;
  • neuroinflammation;
  • neurite biology;
  • brain injury models. Pasted text

Claims of improved memory or prevention of neurodegenerative disease are not established by the supplied evidence.

Inflammatory and Oxidative-Stress Research

NAD-dependent pathways may influence inflammatory signalling through interactions involving sirtuins, NF-κB, and cellular redox systems.

The supplied material describes research involving inflammatory mediators such as TNF-α and IL-6. Pasted text

Metabolic Research

NAD metabolism is closely connected with:

  • glucose metabolism;
  • lipid metabolism;
  • AMPK signalling;
  • insulin-related pathways;
  • mitochondrial oxidation. Pasted text

This has made NAD biology important in obesity, metabolic syndrome, insulin-resistance, and diabetes research.

It does not establish injectable NAD+ as an approved metabolic treatment.

Exercise and Skeletal-Muscle Research

Because NAD+/NADH cycling is essential to cellular energy production, NAD-related research also extends into skeletal-muscle physiology and exercise metabolism.

The supplied material discusses mitochondrial density, oxidative capacity, endurance, and recovery-related endpoints. Pasted text

These findings should not be presented as guaranteed performance enhancement.

Liver and Cardiometabolic Research

NAD-related pathways have also been investigated in models involving:

  • hepatic lipid metabolism;
  • mitochondrial β-oxidation;
  • oxidative stress;
  • vascular function;
  • cardiometabolic biology. Pasted text

Human therapeutic benefits are not established by these mechanisms alone.

Circadian Biology

NAD metabolism follows circadian patterns and interacts with clock-related cellular pathways.

The supplied source therefore discusses NAD+ in relation to circadian rhythm and metabolic timing. Pasted text

Claims of improved sleep or hormonal balance should remain research-oriented unless supported by formulation-specific clinical evidence.

Longevity Research

NAD+ levels and NAD-dependent signalling have become major areas of ageing research.

Studies investigate relationships among:

  • mitochondrial function;
  • DNA repair;
  • sirtuins;
  • metabolism;
  • cellular stress;
  • ageing-related decline. Pasted text

Preclinical findings should not be described as proof of human age reversal or lifespan extension.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is NAD+?

NAD+ stands for Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide.

It is an endogenous coenzyme required for numerous cellular redox reactions and plays a central role in energy metabolism and mitochondrial function. Pasted text

Is NAD+ a peptide?

No.

NAD+ is a nucleotide coenzyme, not a peptide.

Therefore, it does not have an amino-acid sequence.

What is the difference between NAD+ and NADH?

NAD+ is the oxidized form, while NADH is the reduced form.

The two continuously cycle between these states during cellular redox reactions and energy metabolism. Pasted text

How does NAD+ work?

NAD+ accepts and transfers electrons during metabolic reactions.

It also serves as a required substrate for several enzyme families, including sirtuins and PARPs, linking NAD biology to metabolism, mitochondrial function, DNA repair, and stress-response signalling. Pasted text

What is NAD+ researched for?

  • mitochondrial function;

tabs.html:
PT-141 10 mg Pen

Product Description

PT-141 (Bremelanotide) is a synthetic melanocortin receptor agonist derived from alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone research and studied primarily for its effects on central sexual-arousal pathways, melanocortin signalling, motivation, and hypothalamic neurobiology.

Unlike compounds that act mainly through peripheral vasodilation, PT-141 works primarily through the central nervous system, particularly melanocortin receptors associated with neural pathways involved in sexual desire and arousal.

Clinical and preclinical research described in the supplied material links PT-141 with activation of MC4R and MC3R, downstream dopaminergic signalling, and limbic-system pathways involved in sexual motivation. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity PT-141 pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Bremelanotide has been clinically investigated and approved in certain jurisdictions for specific sexual-desire indications. However, approval applies to particular authorized formulations, populations, and indications and should not be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity PT-141 pen.

Clinical / Research Status

PT-141 has a meaningful human evidence base compared with many investigational peptides.

The supplied material identifies:

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human randomized clinical research Yes
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory approval Yes, for specific formulations and indications in certain jurisdictions

The source notes that PT-141 / Bremelanotide has undergone controlled clinical investigation and regulatory evaluation for particular sexual-desire indications. Pasted text

That regulatory history should not be generalized to all PT-141 formulations or unapproved uses.

Evidence Type

The supplied material includes research involving:

  • Phase 3 studies in women with HSDD;
  • clinical research in men with erectile dysfunction;
  • rodent hypothalamic models;
  • subcutaneous pharmacokinetic studies;
  • non-human primate behavioural models;
  • healthy-volunteer research;
  • in-vitro melanocortin receptor-binding studies. Pasted text

This gives PT-141 a combination of human, animal, pharmacological, and receptor-level evidence.

Mechanism of Action

PT-141 acts primarily through central melanocortin receptors, especially MC4R and MC3R.

Activation of these receptors in hypothalamic and limbic pathways can influence:

  • sexual motivation;
  • arousal signalling;
  • dopaminergic activity;
  • reward-related neural circuits;
  • behavioural response.

The supplied material distinguishes PT-141 from PDE-5 inhibitors because its mechanism does not primarily depend on nitric-oxide-mediated peripheral vasodilation. Pasted text

Instead, PT-141 acts further upstream through central neural pathways associated with desire and arousal.

MC4R and MC3R Signalling

The supplied material describes PT-141 binding to melanocortin receptors and influencing intracellular cAMP-related signalling.

Research also discusses downstream effects involving dopaminergic pathways and POMC-related hypothalamic systems. Pasted text

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Central Sexual-Arousal Research

PT-141 is primarily studied for its effects on central neural circuits involved in sexual desire and motivation.

Clinical research described by the source has examined desire-related endpoints and satisfying sexual-event measures in controlled populations. Pasted text

This differs from compounds whose main action is peripheral vascular response.

MC4R and MC3R Research

PT-141 interacts primarily with MC4R and MC3R, two receptor subtypes involved in central melanocortin signalling.

Research focuses on how activation of these receptors influences:

  • cAMP signalling;
  • dopamine-related pathways;
  • motivational behaviour;
  • hypothalamic and limbic activity. Pasted text

Dopaminergic Reward-Signalling Research

The source describes PT-141 in relation to mesolimbic dopamine pathways involved in reward anticipation and sexual motivation.

This makes it relevant to experimental research involving the relationship between melanocortin signalling and central motivational circuits. Pasted text

Research Distinct from PDE-5 Inhibitors

PT-141’s mechanism is different from sildenafil-type compounds.

According to the supplied material, PT-141 does not primarily depend on nitric oxide or peripheral smooth-muscle vasodilation.

Instead, it acts through central melanocortin pathways. Pasted text

This mechanistic distinction is important when describing the compound accurately.

Female Sexual-Desire Research

The supplied material references randomized human studies involving women with hypoactive sexual desire research diagnoses.

These trials examined changes in sexual-desire scores and satisfying sexual events. Pasted text

These findings apply to defined clinical populations and should not be generalized beyond the populations and formulations studied.

Male Arousal Research

PT-141 has also been investigated in male research populations.

The supplied source describes changes in erectile response and sexual behaviour associated with central melanocortin activation. Pasted text

This does not make PT-141 interchangeable with conventional vascular erectile-function treatments.

Neuroendocrine Research

The source describes PT-141 as interacting with POMC-associated and melanocortin pathways within the hypothalamus.

These systems influence broader motivational and behavioural signalling beyond sexual response alone. Pasted text

Hormone-Independent Arousal Signalling

PT-141 does not primarily work by directly increasing testosterone or replacing gonadal hormones.

The supplied material therefore positions it as a centrally acting neuroendocrine modulator rather than a hormone-replacement compound. Pasted text

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Premenopausal women with HSDD Increased desire-related scores and satisfying sexual-event measures
Men with erectile dysfunction Increased erectile response independent of primary PDE-5 pathway activity
Rodent hypothalamic models Increased MC4R-associated signalling and dopaminergic activity
Subcutaneous pharmacokinetic research Rapid systemic absorption with central effects reported within hours
Female non-human primate models Increased solicitation and proceptive behaviour
Healthy volunteer research Predictable systemic exposure following subcutaneous administration
In-vitro receptor-binding studies Activity at MC4R and MC3R with lower MC1R involvement

These findings span clinical, animal, and cellular research and should be interpreted according to the exact formulation and study population used. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving:

  • PT-141 + Kisspeptin-10;
  • PT-141 + Oxytocin;
  • PT-141 + Selank;
  • PT-141 + Tesamorelin. Pasted text

The theoretical research rationale involves combining melanocortin signalling with reproductive, emotional, anxiolytic, or metabolic pathways.

However, the supplied evidence does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated only as experimental research concepts.

Protocol / Dosage Information

The supplied source discusses experimental quantities ranging from approximately 0.5 mg to 2 mg. Pasted text

Its original click calculations were based on a different 10 mg / 2 mL formulation, so those values must not be copied into the Atlas Longevity 3 mL system.

The table above simply translates quantities appearing in the supplied research material into the Atlas pen concentration.

Possible Side Effects

The supplied material reports several adverse effects observed in PT-141 / Bremelanotide research.

These include:

  • nausea;
  • facial flushing;
  • skin warmth;
  • temporary increases in blood pressure;
  • reciprocal decreases in heart rate;
  • headache;
  • dizziness;
  • darkening of pigmented skin areas with repeated exposure. Pasted text

Blood Pressure and Heart Rate

The source specifically reports temporary blood-pressure increases accompanied by decreases in heart rate.

Because these are measurable cardiovascular effects, they should not be minimized as merely cosmetic or insignificant reactions.

Pigmentation Changes

PT-141 is derived from melanocortin research and can interact with pathways related to pigmentation.

Repeated exposure may therefore produce darkening of existing pigmented areas in some research observations. Pasted text

How does PT-141 work?

PT-141 primarily activates melanocortin receptors in the central nervous system, especially MC4R and MC3R.

This influences neural signalling associated with sexual motivation, arousal, and dopaminergic pathways. Pasted text

Is PT-141 a PDE-5 inhibitor?

Selank 10 mg Pen

Product Description

Selank is a synthetic regulatory heptapeptide derived from research into tuftsin, an endogenous immunomodulatory peptide. It is primarily investigated in the areas of stress-response biology, anxiety-related behaviour, neurotransmitter regulation, neuroimmune signalling, and cognitive performance.

Unlike classical benzodiazepines, Selank is not described as a direct GABA-A receptor agonist. Instead, experimental research suggests that it may influence GABAergic tone, serotonin and dopamine metabolism, neurotrophic signalling, and stress-related gene expression through regulatory mechanisms. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity Selank pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Selank remains an investigational neuropeptide. Human research exists, but it is limited and regionally concentrated, so Selank should not be presented as an approved treatment for anxiety disorders, depression, cognitive impairment, stress, or other neurological conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The supplied material describes Selank as being studied primarily in neurobehavioral and anxiolytic research, with limited human clinical investigation alongside more extensive animal and laboratory research. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human controlled research Limited / regional
Human observational research Limited
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Regulatory therapeutic approval Not established

Human findings should therefore be described as exploratory rather than definitive clinical evidence.

Evidence Type

The supplied material references research involving:

  • anxiety-related clinical studies;
  • rodent elevated plus-maze models;
  • cortical neurotransmitter analysis;
  • hippocampal BDNF research;
  • stress-induced immune models;
  • cognitive performance studies;
  • enkephalin-degradation assays. Pasted text

This evidence spans human, animal, and cellular research, with different levels of relevance to real-world therapeutic outcomes.

Mechanism of Action

Selank is studied primarily as a regulatory neuropeptide rather than a classical direct receptor agonist.

The supplied material describes several potential mechanisms:

  • modulation of GABA turnover;
  • regulation of inhibitory neurotransmission;
  • effects on serotonin pathways;
  • effects on dopamine metabolism;
  • changes in inflammatory cytokine expression;
  • modulation of neurotrophic factors;
  • stress-response signalling. Pasted text

GABAergic Regulation

Selank is not described as binding directly to GABA-A receptors in the same way as benzodiazepines.

Instead, experimental studies suggest that it may influence the regulation and turnover of GABA-related signalling.

Monoamine Signalling

Research also describes changes involving serotonin and dopamine metabolism, particularly under experimental stress conditions.

Neuroimmune Signalling

Gene-expression studies referenced by the source suggest potential effects on inflammatory and neurotrophic pathways, creating interest in the interaction between immune signalling and brain function.

These mechanisms remain under investigation and should not be presented as established therapeutic effects in humans.

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

GABAergic Signalling Research

One of the central research areas for Selank is its possible influence on GABA-related inhibitory signalling.

Animal and limited human research have investigated whether Selank can modify GABA turnover without producing the same direct receptor activation associated with benzodiazepines. Pasted text

The supplied material describes reduced anxiety-related measures with less pronounced motor impairment in experimental settings.

This does not establish Selank as an approved anxiolytic medicine.

Serotonin and Dopamine Research

Selank has also been investigated for potential effects on monoamine neurotransmission.

The supplied source discusses changes in serotonin and dopamine metabolism, transporter expression, and receptor-related signalling under stress conditions. Pasted text

These findings remain primarily mechanistic and exploratory.

Anxiety-Related Research

Limited clinical research has examined Selank in populations with anxiety-related symptoms.

The supplied material describes reductions in anxiety scoring measures and preservation of attention or cognition in some studies. Pasted text

The evidence is not sufficient to describe Selank as a universally established treatment for anxiety disorders.

Stress-Response Biology

Animal research has investigated Selank’s potential influence on the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and stress-related corticosterone responses. Pasted text

This makes Selank relevant to research examining the interaction between stress hormones, neurotransmitters, and behavioural responses.

Neuroimmune Research

The supplied source describes gene-expression changes involving inflammatory cytokines and neuroimmune pathways.

This has created research interest in possible connections among:

  • neural signalling;
  • inflammation;
  • immune regulation;
  • stress responses. Pasted text

These findings should not be interpreted as proof that Selank treats inflammatory or immune disease.

Cognitive Performance Under Stress

Experimental research has examined Selank in memory, attention, and executive-function tasks conducted under stress.

The source reports preservation or improvement of certain cognitive measures in selected models. Pasted text

This does not establish Selank as a clinically proven cognitive enhancer.

Non-Sedative Anxiolytic Research

An important research characteristic of Selank is its reported lack of pronounced sedation in certain models.

The supplied source describes relatively preserved motor coordination and reaction time compared with more strongly sedating anxiolytic compounds. Pasted text

This remains a research observation rather than a guarantee of no sedation or impairment.

Neuroplasticity Research

The source also references changes in BDNF-related expression, which has generated interest in Selank’s potential effects on neuroplasticity and neuronal adaptation. Pasted text

Most of this evidence is preclinical.

Research Data

Study / Model Reported Finding
Anxiety-related clinical research Reduced anxiety scores with less sedation reported in selected studies
Rat elevated plus-maze Reduced anxiety-like behaviour and increased open-arm exploration
Rodent cortical neurotransmitter analysis Changes in GABA turnover and serotonin/dopamine metabolism

Stress-induced immunosuppression models Changes in interferon and cytokine balance
Cognitive-performance research Changes in attention, memory and mental-performance measures
Enkephalin degradation assays Reduced enkephalin breakdown in experimental systems

These findings come from different research models and should not all be interpreted as established human clinical benefits. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving Selank with:

  • Semax;
  • BPC-157;
  • Cerebrolysin;
  • NAD+. Pasted text

The proposed research rationale involves combining stress-response, neurotrophic, regenerative, or cellular-energy pathways.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

Possible Side Effects

The supplied material describes Selank as generally well tolerated in animal and limited human research, but the available evidence is not sufficient to establish a complete long-term safety profile.

Reported observations include:

  • mild drowsiness;
  • temporary fatigue;
  • headache;
  • light-headedness;
  • localized redness;
  • injection-site irritation. Pasted text

The source also mentions nasal discomfort associated with intranasal research, which should not automatically be applied to an Atlas pen formulation.

Sedation and Cognitive Effects

The source reports less pronounced sedation or cognitive impairment than classical anxiolytic compounds in available research.

However, this should not be interpreted as proof that Selank can never cause drowsiness, reduced alertness, or cognitive effects.

Dependence and Withdrawal

The supplied source states that dependence and withdrawal have not been observed in the available research data.

Because human studies are limited, absence of a signal should not be interpreted as proof of zero dependence or withdrawal risk under every exposure pattern.

Important areas of uncertainty include:

  • long-term repeated systemic exposure;
  • psychiatric medication interactions;
  • other CNS-active compounds;
  • pregnancy and reproductive exposure;
  • neurological disorders;
  • chronic psychiatric conditions;
  • combination protocols.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Selank?

Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid regulatory peptide derived from tuftsin-related research.

It is primarily investigated for potential effects involving stress responses, GABAergic signalling, monoamine regulation, cognition, and neuroimmune pathways. Pasted text

Is Selank a benzodiazepine?

No.

Selank is a peptide and is not a benzodiazepine.

The supplied research specifically distinguishes its mechanism from direct GABA-A receptor agonism.

How does Selank work?

Selank is studied for potential regulatory effects on:

  • GABA turnover;
  • serotonin metabolism;
  • dopamine signalling;
  • inflammatory gene expression;
  • BDNF-related pathways;
  • stress-response systems. Pasted text

Its exact clinical significance in humans remains under investigation.

Does Selank directly activate GABA receptors?

The supplied source states that Selank does not directly bind GABA-A receptors in the same way as classical benzodiazepine compounds.

Instead, it is researched for its ability to influence GABAergic regulation indirectly. Pasted text

What is Selank researched for?

Research areas include:

  • anxiety-related behaviour;
  • stress response;
  • GABA signalling;
  • serotonin and dopamine regulation;
  • neuroimmune signalling;
  • BDNF expression;
  • attention and memory;
  • cognitive performance under stress.

Human evidence remains limited.

Has Selank been studied in humans?

Yes.

The supplied material references limited clinical research, including anxiety-related studies and comparative research involving medazepam. Pasted text

However, the human evidence base is much smaller than that of established anxiolytic medicines.

Is Selank approved for anxiety?

The supplied material does not establish broad regulatory approval of Selank as a treatment for anxiety disorders.

Its use should therefore remain framed as investigational research.

Does Selank cause sedation?

The supplied source describes relatively little sedation in available studies compared with classical anxiolytic compounds.

However, mild drowsiness and fatigue are also listed among reported observations. Pasted text

Therefore, describing Selank as completely non-sedating would be too strong.

Is Selank addictive?

The supplied source reports no observed dependence or withdrawal in the research it references.

The limited size of the human evidence base means this should not be interpreted as definitive proof of zero dependence potential.

Is Selank researched for cognition?

Yes.

Experimental studies described by the source have investigated attention, memory, cognitive stability, and performance under stress.

These findings do not establish Selank as an approved cognitive enhancer.

What is BDNF and why is it relevant to Selank research?

BDNF — brain-derived neurotrophic factor — is involved in neuronal survival, adaptation, and neuroplasticity.

The supplied source references experimental research reporting changes in BDNF-related expression following Selank exposure. Pasted text

After administration, the dial returns to zero while the unused formulation remains inside the cartridge.

Can Selank be combined with Semax?

Validated human combination safety, efficacy, compatibility, and dosing are not established by the supplied material.

This remains a research concept rather than an established clinical combination.

Semax + Selank Blend Peptide Pen Bali

Dual-Neuropeptide Research Formulation

The Atlas Longevity Semax + Selank Blend Pen combines two experimental peptides studied in different areas of neurological and neurochemical research.

Semax is a synthetic peptide derived from a fragment of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).

Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide developed from the naturally occurring peptide tuftsin.

Both have been investigated in preclinical and limited clinical research, although the quality and applicability of available evidence vary.

The safety and effectiveness of this specific pre-mixed combination have not been established through adequate human clinical trials.

Both variations contain equal quantities of Semax and Selank by mass.

What Is Semax?

Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide derived from a fragment of ACTH.

Researchers have investigated Semax in relation to:

  • Neurotrophic signalling
  • Learning and memory processes
  • Neurochemical regulation
  • Neuronal stress responses
  • Neuroprotection-related mechanisms
  • Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) signalling

Some experimental studies have explored Semax in neurological models, but the evidence does not establish broad clinical effectiveness for cognitive enhancement.

What Is Selank?

Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide related to tuftsin.

It has been investigated in research involving:

  • Stress-response pathways
  • Anxiety-related behavioural models
  • Neurotransmitter signalling
  • Immune and neuroimmune interactions
  • Emotional regulation mechanisms
  • Central nervous system activity

Available findings are not sufficient to establish Selank as a universally safe or effective treatment for anxiety, stress or cognitive conditions.

Why Are Semax and Selank Studied Together?

Semax and Selank have different molecular structures and have been investigated in overlapping areas of neurological research.

Semax research has frequently examined neurotrophic and neuronal signalling.

Selank research has frequently examined stress-related and neuroimmune pathways.

Their combination may be of scientific interest, but this does not establish synergistic effects or superior clinical outcomes.
