Semax 30 mg Pen

Product Description

Semax is a synthetic neuroactive heptapeptide derived from adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-fragment research and studied primarily for its potential effects on neuroplasticity, cognitive signalling, neuroprotection, stress-response biology, and monoaminergic neurotransmission.

Unlike full ACTH, Semax is described in the supplied research material as producing neurological signalling effects without significantly stimulating adrenal corticosteroid production. Experimental research has examined its influence on brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), dopamine, serotonin, synaptic plasticity, neuronal survival, and stress-related gene expression. Pasted text

The source characterizes Semax as having limited human clinical investigation alongside animal and in-vitro research, including studies involving cognition and neurological recovery. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity Semax pen contains 30 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Semax remains an investigational neuropeptide and should not be presented as an approved treatment for stroke, cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, neurological injury, or other medical conditions.

Clinical / Research Status

The supplied material describes Semax as having been studied in cognitive and neuroprotective research settings, including regional clinical applications, while much of the supporting evidence remains animal or mechanistic. Pasted text

Evidence Type Status Based on Supplied Material
Human clinical research Limited / regional
Human observational research Yes
Animal research Yes
In-vitro research Yes
Broad regulatory therapeutic approval Not established by supplied material

The source indicates some human clinical work, but the reference list supplied later is predominantly animal, in-vitro, or observational. For that reason, Atlas content should avoid overstating the strength of controlled human evidence.

Evidence Type

The supplied research includes:

  • neurological clinical studies;
  • ischemic stroke research;
  • rat cerebral-ischemia models;
  • hippocampal neurotrophic-factor studies;
  • cognitive-performance research;
  • chronic-stress animal models;
  • neuronal cell cultures;
  • optic-nerve research. Pasted text

The evidence base therefore combines clinical observations with substantial preclinical research.

Mechanism of Action

Semax is studied primarily for its potential effects on neurotrophic signalling and monoaminergic neurotransmission.

The supplied material describes several proposed mechanisms:

  • increased BDNF-related signalling;
  • modulation of neuronal survival pathways;
  • changes in synaptic plasticity;
  • effects on dopamine signalling;
  • effects on serotonin pathways;
  • changes in stress-related gene expression;
  • neuroimmune and inflammatory modulation. Pasted text

BDNF and Neuroplasticity

BDNF is a neurotrophic factor involved in neuronal survival, synaptic adaptation, and plasticity.

Experimental Semax research has reported changes in BDNF expression, providing one of the central mechanistic rationales for cognitive and neuroprotective investigation.

Monoaminergic Signalling

Semax has also been investigated for effects on dopamine and serotonin systems, particularly under stress or neurological challenge.

ACTH-Related Structure Without Full ACTH Activity

Although Semax originates from ACTH-fragment research, the source describes it as lacking the corticosteroid-stimulating activity associated with full ACTH.

This distinction allows researchers to investigate neurological pathways without relying on full endocrine ACTH activity. Pasted text

Potential Benefits / Research Areas

Neurotrophic-Factor Research

One of the major research areas for Semax involves BDNF and related neurotrophic pathways.

The supplied material reports increased BDNF expression in experimental models and links this with:

  • neuronal survival;
  • dendritic signalling;
  • synaptic plasticity;
  • learning-related pathways. Pasted text

These findings should not be presented as guaranteed cognitive improvement in humans.

Synaptic Plasticity and Memory Research

Semax has been investigated in models involving:

  • memory consolidation;
  • executive function;
  • attention;
  • learning-related signalling;
  • synaptic adaptation.

The source discusses CREB-associated pathways and changes in synaptic density in experimental research. Pasted text

Dopamine and Serotonin Research

The supplied material describes Semax as influencing dopamine and serotonin turnover.

These monoamine systems participate in attention, motivation, mood, reward, and stress-response biology. Pasted text

This does not establish Semax as a treatment for depression, ADHD, or other psychiatric disorders.

Ischemia and Neuroprotection Research

Semax has been investigated in experimental models of cerebral ischemia.

The source reports findings involving:

  • neuronal survival;
  • infarct-related measurements;
  • oxidative-stress markers;
  • glutamate-related excitotoxicity;
  • neurological recovery. Pasted text

Most mechanistic evidence remains preclinical, and Semax should not be presented as an established stroke therapy based on the supplied information.

Gene-Expression Research

Gene-expression studies referenced by the source describe changes in:

  • inflammatory mediators;
  • stress-response proteins;
  • neuronal signalling pathways;
  • neurotrophic factors. Pasted text

This makes Semax relevant to experimental neuroimmune and neuroplasticity research.

Cognitive Resilience Under Stress

Semax has also been investigated in acute and chronic stress models.

The supplied material describes changes in cognitive performance and behavioural outcomes under stress exposure. Pasted text

This should be described as research into cognitive resilience rather than guaranteed enhancement.

Neuroendocrine Selectivity Research

The source highlights the fact that Semax does not appear to produce the same corticosteroid stimulation as full ACTH.

This has made it useful in research attempting to separate ACTH-fragment neurological signalling from adrenal endocrine stimulation. Pasted text

Rat hippocampal tissue Increased BDNF and NGF-related expression
Healthy human cognitive research Changes in attention, memory consolidation and performance under fatigue
Chronic-stress rodent models Reduced anxiety-related behaviours and changes in HPA-axis activity
In-vitro neuronal culture Changes in dopamine/serotonin signalling and oxidative-stress resistance
Optic-nerve models Increased retinal ganglion-cell survival and visual-response markers

These findings span clinical and preclinical research and should not all be interpreted as established human therapeutic outcomes. Pasted text

Potential Stack / Combination Research

The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving:

  • Semax + Selank;
  • Semax + Cerebrolysin;
  • Semax + NAD+;
  • Semax + Dihexa. Pasted text

The proposed research rationale involves combining neurotrophic, stress-response, neurotransmitter, or cellular-energy pathways.

However, the supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore remain experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

The supplied material describes Semax as generally well tolerated in the research it references, but the available human evidence is limited.

Reported observations include:

The source also lists nasal irritation or burning, but that effect relates specifically to intranasal administration and should not automatically be transferred to the Atlas pen.

The source states that significant hormonal, cardiovascular, or systemic adverse effects were not identified in the research it references.

However, it also acknowledges that long-term safety remains under investigation. Pasted text

Important uncertainties include:

  • prolonged systemic exposure;
  • interactions with psychiatric medications;

tabs.html:
Semax 10mg + Selank 10mg Blend Bali

The Semax + Selank 20mg Blend combines two well-known synthetic research peptides in one formulation.

Each vial contains:

Semax — 10mg
Selank — 10mg
Total — 20mg

Semax and Selank have been studied separately for their interactions with neurological and neurochemical pathways. Combining them provides researchers with both peptides in a convenient 1:1 formulation.

What’s Inside?

Semax — 10mg

Semax is a synthetic peptide derived from a fragment of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).

Research involving Semax has explored areas including:

• Neuroplasticity
• Cognitive processes
• Memory and learning pathways
• Neurotrophic signalling
• Neurological research

Selank — 10mg

Selank is a synthetic peptide related to tuftsin, a naturally occurring immunomodulatory peptide.

Research involving Selank has explored:

• Stress-related pathways
• Anxiety-related models
• Neurotransmitter signalling
• Cognitive processes
• Neurological research

Total Blend — 20mg

The formulation contains an equal 1:1 ratio:

10mg Semax + 10mg Selank = 20mg total

Research Areas

The Semax + Selank combination may be of interest for research involving:

• Cognitive signalling
• Neuroplasticity
• Memory and learning pathways
• Stress-response pathways
• Neurotransmitter systems
• Neurotrophic signalling
• Experimental neuroscience

These are research areas and should not be interpreted as established therapeutic benefits.

Semax vs Selank

Although frequently discussed together, Semax and Selank are different peptides.

Semax is primarily associated with research into cognitive, neurotrophic and neuroprotective signalling.

Selank is primarily associated with research into stress, anxiety-related models and neurotransmitter signalling.

This blend contains equal amounts of both compounds.
